#4285. PUBG's extraction shooter spin-off, Black Budget, is finally going to be playable next month

The most interesting development in the PUBG universe, PUBG: Black Budget, is almost ready to show itself off to a wider group of players.

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

#4284. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 23, 2026

This week has been home to some disheartening news. BioWare, the creators of games like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, is being shut down amid a flurry of layoffs. It's another frustrating story from a struggling video game industry. Below you will find some of our stories about the legendary developer, including our massive 2016 oral history. And then after that, you can read about our recommendations of what to play this weekend.

I spent the early hours playing Final Fantasy Resonance trying to figure out precisely why I couldn't put it down. I eventually realized that the game manages in a very purposeful way to answer that quiet need I've so frequently had: "I wish I could experience a game just like Final Fantasy IV or VI again, for the first time, but with a new cast and story." That's pretty much what you can expect here; Resonance is a very purposeful throwback experience that harkens to the early days of FF pixel adventures, but with several modern conveniences, graphical flourishes, and depth added into the mix. It's a big and refreshingly wholesome journey of entertaining party members, summoning giant creatures, flying an airship across the world, and fighting turn-based battles that include absurd spell effects. It's one of my favorite games of the year, and well worth the time it will take to explore. Read our full review for more.

Expect to hear a lot of people proclaiming this as "one of the good ones," as Modern Warfare came out swinging this week with a strong campaign, compelling additions to competitive multiplayer, and an impressive extraction shooter mode in the form of DMZ. I've already been impressed by the first few hours of the campaign, which offers a tense, harrowing, and often disturbingly brutal story that bounces between a number of character perspectives. The gunplay feels tuned in, the traversal and melee is satisfying, and the narrative beats grounded in excellent actin performances. Our reviewer has spent even more time with the full game, and can share their full perspective to help inform whether you want to take a dive into this year's installment.

The Nintendo Sports franchise, which began with Wii Sports in 2006, has never been about the single-player experience. That remains true 20 years later in Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. But this time around, Nintendo has boosted the amount of content beyond what the series has typically provided, appealing to all player counts, all while retaining its trademark approachability. Whether you're joining together with three friends for some friendly competition across the package's 12 sports or you're trying to climb the Island Crown ladder by beating increasingly difficult single-player opponents, Switch Sports Resort is a great motion-controlled collection.

Halloween is around the corner. As you’re buying overpriced candy, deciding which version of the Joker to dress up as, and debating between watching Obsession and Backrooms over a cup of cider, it’s the perfect time to replay old horror games or dive into new ones. 2026 has a solid roster of choices for the latter thanks to releases like Resident Evil Requiem, Paranormasight: The Mermaid’s Curse, and Silent Hill: Townfall, but Tenebris Somnia shouldn’t be overlooked if you’re looking for a cool indie throwback.

Part retro-inspired adventure game, part live-action indie horror film, you’ll uncover the mystery of a nightmare-induced apartment building and battle horrors to rescue your trapped ex. The gameplay is survival horror 101, but it’s executed well, with consistently clever and inventive puzzle-solving as a highlight. It may not be a graphical powerhouse, but Tenebris Somnia still maintains a creepy atmosphere thanks to solid scares partly delivered by effective and well-made live-action cinematics. If you’re going to binge horror films, you may as well play one too. You can read my full review here.

Full disclosure: I have not played One Piece: Grand Gourmet. I was trying to finish up Castlevania: Belmont's Curse when a review game landed in my lap that I've had to give my full attention. That said, I have watched a lot of the One Piece anime, have a cat named Nami, and dog named Luffy.

I don't know if One Piece: Grand Gourmet is any good, but I like the premise and pixel graphics. One Piece is a very malleable franchise (which is why its live action adaptation is pretty good), so the idea of managing a restaurant as Sanji feels like it could be a very good fit. I plan on climbing aboard with all my hopes and dreams soon. And it is out now, which is good to know.

Similar to the entry above, I have not yet played Stupid Never Dies yet (there are too many video games!), but we like to use this weekly article to call out the new video games of the week. I am eager to check out Stupid Never Dies primarily because of its pop-punk soundtrack and 2000s aesthetic. I think it has the potential to be a fun, nostalgic throwback to my youth when I was learning Blink-182's "Dammit" on guitar and playing Devil May Cry.

The Blood of Dawnwalker has been out for just over seven weeks now, but I wouldn't blame you if you haven't finished it – or even started it – yet. A lot has come out! But if you need a reason to jump back in, this week's 1.1 update is a great excuse – the devs have added hundreds of bug fixes and other minor improvements, so it should run better than it ever did before. There's also an even easier difficulty mode if you want to cruise through without worrying about combat, and a new in-game potion that lets you respec all your skill points. I stalled out about halfway through (when I started playing Wolverine), but I'm planning to jump back in this weekend.

Oh, and you can pet dogs and cats now. Maybe I should have led with that.

Multiplayer physics mountain-climbing game Peak became one of the most viral co-op experiences of 2025 (I refuse to use the term friendslop), but only PC players have enjoyed its wacky shenanigans. That changed this week as Peak is now available on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Switch 2. Either alone or, preferably, alongside up to three friends, you’ll try to ascend procedurally generated, absurdly unrealistic mountains riddled with dangers. Working together is key, a tricky prospect thanks to the in-game proximity chat that necessitates sticking together, but griefing each other, intentionally or otherwise, is just as entertaining – maddeningly frustrating at times, but entertaining. Peak on consoles includes all post-launch content and, best of all, supports crossplay for all platforms.

The original Azul remains one of my all-time favorite games even after many years, but it just misses the bar with its strategic complexity to be one I'd pull out to play with the kids. That why I was especially delighted to find that Azul Kids is one of those rare "adapted for children" projects that turned out extremely well.

Players take on the roll of creative young artists building mosaic displays with various colored tiles. The concept remains simple enough to work for even very young players of age five or six, but the whole family should have fun with the approachable strategy implications of choosing tiles and completing your masterpiece.

Bad signal or dead zones? Download your issues before you leave and read anywhere.

#4283. Dragon boy Durin is the star of the show in Genshin Impact's wintry Luna 3 update, launching in early December

Genshin Impact is getting two new characters and a whole host of new content in Version Luna 3, which arrives in under two weeks.

The latest HoYoverse Special Program has brought us big Genshin Impact news. Version Luna 3 has been fully revealed, continuing the Nod-Krai story. The new chapter arrives December 3 across all platforms.

The Moon-Prayer Night is the big in-world festival, marking Dameselette's final night before she sets off for the moon. The new update, of course, introduces new playable characters, one with an interesting mechanic.

The events of this new chapter take place following Rarcher of Solnari’s defeat. The victory has given way to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations, which brings various stalls to the Nasha Town, alongside a new souvenir stamp book where you can record your memories.

All is not fine, however, as Alice and Nicole Reeyn come bearing some bad news about phantoms appearing across the Nod-Krai region at Teyvat's borders. There’s a mystery to be uncovered here, and your journey to do so won’t be a lonely one.

The highly-anticipated Durin is at last the new playable character. A 5-Star Pyro Sword wielder, Durin can switch between two different forms: one lets him deal damage, while the other is best suited to supporting the team.

Durin was once a dragon, you see, who was later given a human body. This is why he’s able to switch forms. The more powerful, Abyssal-infused form can launch major attacks on single targets to boost his own Vaporize and Melt damage, while his support form reduces enemies’ Elemental Resistance and deals AoE Pyro damage.

Durin’s Story Quest will shed more light on that aspect of his life, and completing it earns you a reward for him. Speaking of quests, completing the Archon Quest will grant you 500 Primogems. As a member of Hexenzirkel, Durin and other characters can gain new powers when you complete more quests in Moon-Prayer Night.

All characters connected to the Hexenzirkel can benefit from certain story quests tied to their abilities. This is a big new addition, and will affect Venti, Klee, Albedo, Mona, Razor, Fischl, and Sucrose - all of whom can become Hexerei characters. This ties into the new Hexerei Secret Rite effect, which will trigger when two or more Hexerei characters are present. The effect boosts the entire party’s combat effectiveness.

The other new character in Luna 3 is Jahoda, a 4-Star Anemo Bow wielder who’s great at healing teammates and absorbing Elements, which she can then use to deal damage. The first phase of Luna 3 will feature Durin and Jahoda, alongside the return of Venti. The second phase sees no new character debuts, but does feature the return of Varesa and Xilonen.

There’s more to get excited about in Luna 3, even if you don’t feel like spending most of your time in Nod-Krai. The Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event will take you back to Dragonspine, where you’ll find winter-theme minigames appropriate to an update cycle spanning December to January. This is how you can earn the 4-Star Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow, too.

Beyond that, you can also look forward to the Miliastra Wonderland UGC module getting new updates. The Wonderland Resource Center is where creators can get and share resources through the editing tool.

#4282. Maya Hawke Reportedly Cast In MTG Movie, And Fans Are Sure They Know Who She's Playing

Magic: The Gathering might have just found its Chandra Nalaar, as Maya Hawke has reportedly been cast in the upcoming film, directed by Matt Johnson. This report comes via Deadline, which says it has sources who confirmed the casting but not the specific role. However, Magic fans believe there can be only one choice for Hawke, whose most recent role is in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

This is admittedly a huge name to attach to the project, and while it should come as no surprise given how stacked the Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves cast was, some believed this project would be scaled back in comparison because of its box office struggles. As far as statement castings go, if this report is accurate, recruitment for the Magic movie is off to a great start.

Credibility will be huge for the Magic: The Gathering film, and this reported casting of Maya Hawke brings it in spades. Fresh off the huge success of Stranger Things and being part of The Hunger Games franchise, director Matt Johnson couldn't have found a much bigger star right now to have attached to the project.

Deadline says the film is expected to have an "ensemble feel," which also helped the D&D movie's wider appeal, rather than relying on one major name and then casting relative unknowns around them. This report also states that Maya Hawke was offered the role outright without needing to go through an audition process, which suggests that she is a name that the team behind the film had in mind before the audition process started.

Fans strongly believe that Hawke will portray the iconic pyromancer Chandra Nalaar, a character with strikingly similar facial features to Maya Hawke, as well as similar hair color. It's easy to see why fans have made this connection so quickly, but until there is official confirmation of the casting and role, everything is purely speculative.

Magic: The Gathering is headed to the big screen, and it needs a cast to match.

Ultimately, this casting sets a high bar for the film from the get-go, and while Matt Johnson has said he is a massive Magic: The Gathering fan, writing and directing a movie based on a property with such a ferocious fanbase has to be intimidating.

There will no doubt be countless rounds of fantasy casting now that an actor is finally attached to the project, and fans will also start speculating about the film, because there are so many routes it could take given the 30+ years of lore to draw from.

Realistically, we'd like to see a true origins film that explores the multiverse at a very introductory level, with an exciting story layered on top that introduces us to some of our favorite Planeswalkers in ways we've never seen before. This casting news has us excited, and hopefully we won't have to wait long for more news on actors attached to the project.

#4281. Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds - Year Two 2.0.0 Patch Now Live - New Additions, Changes & Improvements

Update [Wed 4th Nov 2026, 1:15am]: The Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds Year Two Update (Version 2.0.0) has now gone live. It kicks off with the Godzilla Pack, which is the first paid Year Two DLC. Bayonetta also joins the race today as the first free character update of Year Two.

Here's the full rundown about this update via Sega's website (the patch notes are huge!):

On this page: Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds - Version 2.0.0

Duels let you take on other racers in 1-on-1 showdowns. This mode can be played both offline and online. While racing, you'll have an extra ace up your sleeve: Duel Boost. This gauge fills up as time passes and you use items. Once it's full, press the button to boost ahead. Time your Duel Boost well to pull off clutch comebacks!

Face off against CPU CrossOver racers in offline 1-on-1 matches. By defeating these powerful rivals, you'll earn unique rewards. Keep on progressing to unlock the new racer Bayonetta!

Test your skills in a 1-on-1 match against players worldwide. Give it everything you've got in an adrenaline-pumping race where it's just you, your opponent, and the track.

Compete for the most points within a limited number of races. Join these limited-time events and earn Duel Medals. Exchange them for exclusive horns, auras, and other rewards!

Face off against a friend or family member with this Friend Match option. *On Nintendo Switch™ and Nintendo Switch™ 2, you can play this mode in Local Wireless.

The Super Slot amplifies the effects of your Gadgets. *To use the Super Slot, you must first unlock the Grand Master Plate by racing at least 40 times. Players who have already fulfilled these conditions will be able to use the Super Slot upon installing the patch.

We're adding various missions that you can complete by playing regularly. Clear them by the deadline to earn Donpa Tickets and Duel Medals. *You must be connected to the Internet to participate in Play Missions.

Exchange your Donpa Tickets and Duel Medals for auras, horns, decals, characters, titles, and Jukebox tracks at the new in-game Shop. We'll be updating the store lineup over time.

Free Matches* don't affect your rank, so feel free to jump in without any pressure.

*Head over to Ranked Match for the original World Match experience.

Matchmaking will now pit you against Rivals of similar skill level. Come out on top to earn bonus Donpa Tickets!

We've overhauled the main menu to make room for all the new modes. Now when you select World Match, Legend Competition, Ranked Match, and Free Match will show up as options.

All new Festivals will be 10 days instead of 3. There's more time to join the fun and rack up all of the Festival Point Rewards.

Alongside the extended Festivals, win streaks will now determine Festival Rankings rather than Festival Points. When a Festival is live, your longest win streak will appear on the leaderboard. If your team finishes in 2nd place, don't worry. Your win streak won't reset, allowing you to keep up your run.

AI Rival teams can now appear in your matches at random. Defeating them earns you bonus Festival Points!

Win even more crowns while playing Festivals!

Awarded to players who have a 5+ win streak.

These can be obtained once your Gadget Plate reaches Grand Master Plate or higher.

The following Gadgets, previously distributed as Festival rewards, can now be purchased* with Donpa Tickets from the Customize Gadgets screen.

*These can be purchased once your Gadget Plate reaches Master Plate or higher.

Super Slot added: Powering up the Gadget System

The Super Slot, the 7th Gadget slot, gives players even more ways to customize their racing strategy.

Alongside this addition, we've adjusted underpowered and overpowered Gadgets.

We've also introduced 1-slot variants of existing Gadgets that are compatible with the Super Slot.

To add more ways to drive, the update adds Mod Gadgets, which offer bigger stat bonuses than existing Tuner Gadgets, and the new Charge Gadgets.

Plus, we've adjusted the overall balance, shortening the time it takes Rings to spawn and buffing Acceleration Type Machines.

These changes will give racers in the middle of the pack chances to stage a comeback.

Going forward, more Gadget and Machine adjustments will be made based on usage and win rates.

Rings now take less time to respawn after players collect them.

In Ver. 1.4, it was difficult to collect Rings when racing alongside others. As a result, Gadgets that let players obtain Rings independently held a significant advantage.

We've implemented this change to shake up the meta, and give players in middle positions more chances for success.

Since these adjustments will make the Ring Engine Gadgets and Ring Evolution more powerful, we have rebalanced their performance accordingly.

*These adjustments do not apply to offline modes, such as Grand Prix and Race Park.

Shortened recovery time after taking damage.

Based on usage and win rates of Acceleration Type Machines, we have made adjustments to improve their signature trait of recovering quickly.

They should excel on courses with many enemies and obstacles, as well as in races where attacks are frequent.

Fixed an issue where Power Type Machines had a higher maximum speed bonus cap than other Machines.

Originally planned for Ver. 1.4.1, we postponed this fix to prevent an issue making it impossible to update your records in Time Trial. However, as the new Gadget Slot is likely to impact records in Ver. 2.0, we have proceeded with this change.

Adjusted Omochao's Ring placement so that Rings are easier to collect mid-jump.

While holding either Boost or Double Boost, the other item can now still spawn from an Item Box. Previously, holding either a Boost or Double Boost made both items less likely to appear.

Adjusted the explosion effect to better match the duration of its attack hitbox.

Adjusted the placement of Rings and Item Boxes to improve the risk-reward balance of certain paths on the following courses:

Since their introduction, Ring Engine and Hyper Ring Engine have maintained high win rates, particularly in Emerald Grade of Legend Competition

Since Ver. 2.0 makes it easier to maintain Rings due to the shortened Ring respawn times and the ability to equip an additional Gadget that grants Rings with the Super Slot, we've lowered the top speed bonus from these two Gadgets.

In parallel, we've adjusted Gadgets that make it easier to maintain your Rings:

Slipstream Bounty, Acceleration Character Kit, Slipstream Kit

The following Ring Gadgets have been enhanced. Since these Gadgets don't continuously collect Rings, these enhancements should have only a small impact on Ring Engine builds:

Increased the number of Rings you can receive from 15 to 25.

Increased the number of Rings you can receive from 4 to 6.

Held off on adjusting Mini Ring Thief due to its use in Ring Engine builds.

Ring Gain Boost/Acceleration Character Kit

The following Driving Gadgets were useful on certain courses and in certain situations, but in many cases ended up being underpowered We have enhanced their performance in Ver. 2.0 to make their unique abilities more distinct:

After a Perfect Landing, the duration of the maximum speed boost now increases proportionate to the number of Air Tricks performed.

Added an effect that makes all Levels charge 1.7x faster while in flight form.

Enhanced the Gadgets below to make them more useful in the current game environment:

Since balance adjustments can weaken Gadgets and make them less viable for setting new records in Time Trial, we may make separate Gadget adjustments for Time Trial alone starting in Ver. 2.0. For Ver. 2.0, the following Gadgets perform differently in Time Trial.

In Time Trial, reduced the top speed bonus for acquiring a Ring has been reduced from 3 km/h to 2 km/h.

*When equipped in the Super Slot, the bonus remains unchanged at 3 km/h.

In Time Trial, this Gadget will have the same performance as in Ver. 1.4. However, you will no longer get an additional stat boost by equipping both the Ring Engine and Hyper Ring Engine. You can get the same boost by equipping Quick Starter or Starting Boost Bounty as your 7th Gadget.

In Time Trial, this Gadget will have the same performance as in Ver. 1.4, and will evolve every 10 Rings.

In Time Trial, this Gadget will have the same performance as in Ver. 1.4.

To commemorate Ver. 2.0, we're launching a login campaign featuring "I ♡" Sonic character decals. Grab your favorite character's decal and deck out your ride! More details coming soon on the Sonic socials.

Decals in partnership with The k4sen, an event held by popular streamer k4sen, are now available.

New Brand Collab Decals! Added collaboration decals from the brands listed below. 3 Yoshinoya Decals 7 Imuraya Decals 3 AUTOBACS Decals

Due to the recent influx of new Gadgets and the introduction of Duel Mode, we've expanded the following customization features.

To make the game more approachable for new players, lowered the unlock requirements for Gadgets and Slots from Bronze Plate onward. These lower requirements will be applied for current players the next time they launch the game.

In addition, to open up more competitive builds early in the game, we've changed the acquisition timing for Slipstream Bounty and Dash Panel Mini Bounty from Gadget Unlock 3 to when Master Plate is unlocked.

The latest version of the game's credits are now live.

We have updated content for future live operations.

In Ver. 2.0, prior to the start of Best-of-10 in Duel Match, "End Challenge" and "Round -1" are displayed.

This issue will be resolved after the first Best-of-10 competition starts.

In addition, if the event period ends while a player still has races remaining in the Best-of-10 competition, "X Tries Remaining" will be displayed even though the event has ended.

This issue will be addressed in a future update. We will let you know as soon as it has been resolved.

Thanks to all the CrossWorlds players out there for rocketing through the multiverse with us throughout the World Championship and our major Year Two update.

We’re committed to delivering new content to keep the game fresh, and we’ll continue making improvements based on your feedback.

Thank you for your continued support of Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds!

Original Story: [Tue 3rd Nov, 2026 00:45 GMT]:

It's another huge week in gaming, and Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds is joining in on the fun with its launch of "Year Two".

This includes a major title update (Version 2.0.0), and ahead of the 3rd November 2026 rollout, Sonic Global Community Director Aaron Webber has outlined what you can expect. It will include "new additions, changes, and improvements".

Of course, there's also the "Year Two" free and paid characters and machines. The free characters announced will include Bayonetta (arriving 3rd November), and she will be followed by McLaren Racing (Sonic) later this month, and Aigis in early 2027.

#4280. The Legacy and Evolution of Rockstar Games: How One Studio Redefined Open-World Gaming

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

I grew up with an unhealthy obsession with the Grand Theft Auto series. The game wasn’t obviously meant for an 8-year-old, but it showed me the greatest gift: my parents wanting to give me happiness and comfort throughout my upbringing, even if it meant unknowingly handing me a game that was clearly meant for older audiences.

But hey, it didn’t meddle with my behavior, alright? Playing San Andreas was one of my most endearing experiences, with countless playthroughs/save files. And I mean, some of my best video game memories even involved my dad helping me clear a couple of tough missions in both it and Vice City. So from those 3D-era entries to see how far Rockstar has come to be this industry powerhouse with their sandbox video game series is genuinely astounding to see.

Aaron Garbut, co-studio head of Rockstar North, explained that no single person has the entire game mapped out in their head.

Rockstar Games has spent decades building some of the most recognisable worlds in video game history. Whether it's the streets of Los Santos, the mob-boss-riddled underworld of Liberty City, or a quiet ride through the unforgiving American frontier with an on-the-run gang of outlaws, there's something remarkably special about the worlds this studio creates.

With Grand Theft Auto VI approaching in just over two weeks, it's worth looking back at how that journey unfolded. From the studio's transformation and the franchises that shaped its identity to the enormous expectations around its next release, Rockstar's legacy is about much more than the games it has sold. It's about how one developer helped redefine what players expect from open-world experiences.

We’re taking this back to the humble beginnings of Rockstar Games. See, before it became one of the most popular names in the gaming landscape, its story actually began with a much smaller development team in Dundee, Scotland. Founded in 1988 by David Jones and a group of fellow developers, DMA Design started as a relatively small studio with ambitions to make its mark in an industry still finding its footing.

Its early releases, including Menace and Blood Money, showed its interest in arcade-inspired action games, but the arrival of a quirky little game called Lemmings in 1991 truly put the developer on the map. This relatively simple puzzle game (unexpectedly) became an enormous success, selling an estimated 20 million copies across its various platforms.

However, a very different kind of project would ultimately change the studio's future, since in 1997, DMA Design would then release the original Grand Theft Auto, trading its familiar arcade experiences for a top-down crime sandbox that allowed you to steal vehicles, complete odd-job missions, evade the police, and wreak havoc across fictional cities.

As the OG Grand Theft Auto continued to gain momentum despite being an experimental first entry, DMA Design underwent a series of ownership changes before becoming part of Take-Two Interactive and the wider Rockstar Games family around the turn of the millennium.

Eventually, the studio relocated from Dundee to Edinburgh, and in 2002, it officially became Rockstar North. This transformation, or turnaround, whichever one you prefer, would soon carry forward the creative foundations established years earlier. And little did you or I know just how far that journey would take them; this small Scottish team was now at the heart of a studio that would go on to produce some of the most influential open-world experiences in gaming history.

Former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij recalls how GTA 3’s small team made communication easier and gave developers room to experiment.

Funnily enough, I had the chance to revisit GTA 3 this past month as part of my replay of all the mainline entries before VI’s arrival. Forgive me if it was the Definitive Edition; it was dirt-cheap on sale, and I’d already played the OG version on my PS2 as a kid, so I thought, why not try things differently, especially after this much time has passed since this trilogy’s controversial release?

Now, contrary to what the header suggests, although open-world games existed long before Grand Theft Auto III arrived, few developers had managed to bring together the same level of freedom, exploration, and interactive storytelling that Rockstar would eventually become known for. In fact, this is also why I’d like to give a shout-out to my co-worker and friend, Maddie, for discussing how 1999's Urban Chaos, developed by Mucky Foot Productions, was already experimenting with a 3D urban environment, free-roaming exploration, and mission-based gameplay two years before GTA 3 hit the PS2.

While it wasn't the expansive sandbox Rockstar would then create in later titles, it showed the potential of this simple yet experimental idea: letting players explore and interact with a full 3D city. But because it went beyond the formulaic approach of the prior two GTAs, you could absolutely make a case that this game was a generational release for its time.

Instead of simply following a predetermined series of missions, players could steal vehicles, explore different neighborhoods, interact with pedestrians, engage in shootouts, and stumble upon all sorts of unexpected chaos along the way. Driving, shooting, and exploring were no longer separate gameplay modes, but seamlessly interconnected parts of a much larger experience.

Oh, and it didn’t stop there, obviously. The game's success would go on to influence countless developers, establishing a formula that would shape much of the open-world genre for years to come, since Rockstar wasn't simply offering players a large map to explore; it was creating an environment filled with activities, distractions, and opportunities for experimentation.

Playing San Andreas was one of my most endearing experiences, with countless playthroughs/save files.

The studio continued refining that approach with Grand Theft Auto: Vice City in 2002 and then Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas in 2004. The former introduced a distinctive 1980s atmosphere reminiscent of Miami Vice’s stylized tone and an unforgettable soundtrack, while the latter expanded the formula considerably with multiple cities, character customization, and RPG-inspired mechanics.

So by the time San Andreas arrived, Rockstar had shown how much freedom and variety could fit into a single open-world experience. It is genuinely insane that these guys released three back-to-back bangers; it's an honest travesty that they outsourced the modern re-release of them to an external developer under their umbrella.

GTA 3 often ran at just 7 or 8 FPS during development, according to former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij.

While Grand Theft Auto remained Rockstar's biggest commercial success, the company was never particularly interested in limiting itself to a single franchise; these guys were seriously trailblazing their way to the top. That’s because throughout the 2000s, its growing network of development studios experimented with different genres, storytelling approaches, and settings, resulting in some of its most memorable cult favorites.

Bully took the familiar open-world formula and turned it into a crude yet charming coming-of-age adventure. Meanwhile, Manhunt explored a much darker side of the company's creativity through its disturbing atmosphere (enough to give me the frights as a kid) and brutal stealth-based gameplay, and then Midnight Club brought open-city exploration into the street racing scene of the 2000s that other series like NFS also capitalized on with Fast and Furious’ popularity.

And don’t worry, like most of you, possibly longtime fans reading this, I still hold an undying grudge against Rockstar for never revisiting these games again, especially the high possibilities for a sequel to Bully, which I’m never burying the hatchet over because the Scholarship Edition is one of my most played and adored games on the Xbox 360. The bottom line is that these projects showed Rockstar's ambitions extended well beyond crime-driven satire sandboxes, allowing its various studios to establish their own identities across genres.

Rockstar Games has spent decades building some of the most recognisable worlds in video game history.

Of course, Grand Theft Auto wasn't going anywhere. And how ironic that I rolled credits on this just a week ago. With GTA IV in 2008, Rockstar took a noticeably different approach to its established formula for a grittier, more grounded portrayal of Liberty City akin to New York City.

It introduced a string of themes like revenge, organized crime overlords butting heads for power, and the often uncomfortable realities of chasing the American Dream. Plus, things like the ragdoll physics and weight-based driving model were the icing on the cake for an otherwise brilliant crime drama, one that I personally think is the best in the series in terms of writing. However, as much as I hate to admit it, Rockstar wasn't finished pushing those boundaries.

An interview with Rockstar reveals details about GTA 6's morality system.

Grand Theft Auto V arrived in 2013, taking you back to Los Santos and introducing three playable protagonists: Michael, Franklin, and Trevor. Its intertwining storytelling, enormous variety of activities, and remarkable sense of freedom made it a defining open-world release of its generation. Today, it is insane to think about how many records this game has broken: it's one of the best-selling video games of all time, second only to Minecraft, and has generated billions of dollars since its original launch.

Beyond the story mode, GTA Online (unfortunately) gradually grew into a massive multiplayer platform of its own, keeping players invested through years of updates, new missions, vehicles, heists, and activities. And I won’t lie: as someone who spent an unhealthy number of hours on it, this game was partly why I found two of my bestest friends. Also, this mode's longevity and the revenue it generated through microtransactions were low-key part of why GTA V became a cultural phenomenon that kept thriving across multiple console generations.

The wizards at Rockstar didn’t stop there, because the leap that came forward after would soon set the benchmark for people to compare most open-world releases to, even if most of those comparisons became insufferable to come across in social media posts and/or videos.

And that considerable leap came when Rockstar dropped the technical bombshell that was Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018. You see, I could’ve put the original entry in the section above with the other projects these guys did, but it only felt right to include it here, since both these two Wild West open-world titles became games that almost felt like companion pieces to the GTA franchise. That was evident not only in the mission design, but also in newer additions like the Honor system, a fully realized wildlife ecosystem, and other gameplay elements that made it feel like a sister game to GTA.

Following the success of the 2010 entry, the sequel offered a story centered around Arthur Morgan and the gradual decline of the Van der Linde gang, one that slowly connected to the events of RDR1. Its greatest achievement, however, was arguably the extraordinary level of detail packed into its bygone world. From real wildlife behavior and daily NPC routines to dynamic world events that shifted depending on the protagonist or time passed, almost every aspect of its world contributed to an incredible sense of immersion.

Although years later, you’ll now find some recent verbal engagements about people arguing about its flawed mission design, and as much as I think it's a bit overrated (please put the pitchforks down), I will wholeheartedly agree on the fact that this was THE game that made Rockstar the rightful heir to the throne for creating one of the most immersive and compelling open-world games of all time. Most importantly, it also rewarded those willing to slow down and simply enjoy their surroundings, and I think that’s the best compliment to give RDR2 given the current attention span of most mainstream audiences.

After decades of refining its approach to open-world design, Rockstar Games now stands on the doorstep of what could be its most ambitious project yet, as GTA VI represents more than just another long-awaited sequel, especially considering how much the studio has accomplished since we first stepped foot into Los Santos by repo’ing cars with Franklin and Lamar or just cruising around Ocean Beach as Tommy.

I won’t bore your ear with a bunch of what-if bumbo jumbo, but all I want to sign off with is that, given everything Rockstar has showcased so far, there's plenty of reason to be excited about the possibilities they could improve upon here, particularly when considering the technical artistry demonstrated in RDR2.

We’ve already seen an extent of the full gameplay in action with the Extended Look, as well as tons of deeper details shared online across media outlets that make this entry a proper sim-like experience, which I honestly don’t mind since I genuinely wanted Rockstar to bring back the RPG stuff they introduced back in San Andreas. Heck, even if it’s not confirmed, throw in vehicle schools again to give Lucia and Jason even more stats to manage.

For me, one of the biggest challenges GTA VI faces is delivering a story that can stand alongside GTA IV because Niko Bellic's journey for me remains one of the franchise's most memorable narratives precisely because it went beyond the usual criminal escapade trope. Most of all, it made its protagonist feel like more than another criminal navigating a fictional city, and I'd love to see Jason and Lucia achieve that in their own way.

Their relationship already gives Rockstar an interesting foundation to explore, but what matters most is whether the studio can make players genuinely care about the people behind all the chaos. Give me another round of NPC social links calling either protagonist just for a round of bowling or, y’know, give me reasons to interact with them again via their special abilities/benefits.

Now, with Leonida and the newly imagined Vice City waiting just around the corner, it feels like we're about to experience the next chapter in a legacy that has shaped how an entire generation experiences video games.

While I generally have mixed feelings about the overly eccentric fanbase, I’ll put that aside for now since I’m also proudly blasting Flower in Hurricane and Inner Light on repeat these days to itch my hype fever for the game’s release on November 19th. Whether Rockstar can deliver another landmark open-world experience remains to be seen, but hey, to anyone who made it here to see it happen, I hope we eat good with whatever they’ve cooked up over the past 13 years.

Rockstar says GTA 6 pre-loading begins November 10 and could require up to 212 GB, though some official pages still show the old date.

#4279. Phantom Blade Zero Review In Progress – Shaping Up To Be One Of The Best Action Games I've Ever Played

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding achievement for the action genre. So astounding that I feel pulled to experience everything it has to offer… and that means instead of rolling credits, I’ve been busy completing story-critical side quests and more to get the most complete ending. That’s another way of saying I am enjoying this game very, very much but still need more time to render a final verdict, which is why you’re reading a review-in-progress of Phantom Blade Zero rather than a scored piece.

Though I’m not interested in guesstimating a score right now, I know it will be high because Phantom Blade Zero impresses and then some. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and I’m shocked to be writing that. This is a debut of sorts for developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile games and smaller-scale titles; it’s the team’s first triple-A release, and its first game of this kind. This studio is so clearly a dedicated student of the genre, analyzing what works here and what works there in other action greats to create something of its own. It looks forward at what action games can do, can play like, can look like, while looking back at the games before it and understanding why those games – games like Devil May Cry, Elden Ring, Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, Bayonetta, and just about every other quality action game you can think of – continue to be ones we hold so highly. Should it stick the landing, Phantom Blade Zero will join that echelon of action pedigree.

Protagonist Soul is a quiet, mostly stoic martial arts master who prefers to let his blades (of which there are so, so many) do the talking. The Order he’s sworn his life to betrays him, and, in an effort to right wrongs, he discovers a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the blood-soaked Chinese martial underground known as Wulin. As a result, puppets, secret sects, powerful god-like creatures, monstrous beasts, and much more prowl Wulin’s various biomes. I haven’t kept count, but there are a massive number of enemies to take down, both standard mob variants and bosses, and the game stays fresh throughout. It's even fresher when you consider how many weapons you can acquire on Soul’s journey.

Every weapon is wholly unique, like picking up a new character in a fighting game, each with its own moveset and abilities. Upgrading these weapons through various tiers unlocks additional abilities, and you can even Soul Temper weapons to add one final, game-changing ability or perk. A fully upgraded weapon can have a moveset that uses the majority of buttons on your controller. You can do the same with Phantom Edges, special tide-turning weapons with limited uses (before you build up additional charges). Combined with different accessories and medicine types, Phantom Blade Zero offers hundreds, perhaps thousands, of combat kit permutations. You can play as a drunken fighter who switches between sober, tipsy, and drunken states, with his range and damage output changing as a result; you can focus on a bleed build, ripping enemies to shreds with charged attacks that utilize Soul's own HP to deal extra damage (that can then be earned back with bleed); you can use lightning, wind, fire, and ice to create elemental storms against enemies, and you can use a sword that switches between different elemental states on command as well. You can also just pound enemies to pulp with Phantom Edge fists, too. I’ve struggled to stop using these fists since acquiring them because they’re so satisfying.

Forty-plus hours into Phantom Blade Zero, it feels like I’ve played as dozens of different Souls because I've discovered so many build types. S-Game smartly pushes you to try new builds and weapons as you get them, doling out generous upgrade materials and currency; it encourages you to try everything, and the next weapon might just become your new favorite.

Finding these materials (and additional fights) is great fun, too, because Phantom Blade Zero’s various open-area biomes are a genuine joy to explore. You are always rewarded for taking the optional path, and those rewards are always worthwhile. You might find a healthy pile of upgrade materials, or a boss with a weapon you’ll fall in love with. The way buildings, alleys, caves, cliffsides, and other environmental features weave in and out of each other evokes FromSoftware’s architectural design and the subsequent shortcut “aha!” moments.

That said, Phantom Blade Zero is definitively not a Soulslike, though you’d be forgiven for assuming as much given its challenging suite of bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, which are this game’s equivalent of bonfires. However, its challenge is much more surmountable (with various difficulties and accessories to ease parry and dodge timing), and its world progression is materially different. Kill an enemy and it’s dead for good, which to my surprise, adds a sense of worldbuilding I didn’t know I wanted. Progression through this journey feels tangible because I’m actually removing traces of evil with my weapons, traces that don’t respawn when I interact with checkpoints. It’s a nice change of pace that narratively speaks to Soul’s efforts.

Along the way, countless reading materials shed light on Phantom Blade Zero’s intertwining stories, and tracking down the next memory, scroll, or book entry rewards you if you’re interested in the full picture of this Wuxia story. I’d argue the game’s story is its weakest element, but only when compared to the rest of the package. It doesn't break any new ground narratively, but it provides enough mystery and thrill to keep things moving. And while performances are great, talking to characters is still mostly just two people standing across from each other talking through a new quest. Fortunately, cutscenes pick up the slack with dramatic villains, heartfelt revelations, raw tension, and more.

Production value is high across the board, thanks to incredibly impressive animation and a beautiful rendering of this dark fantasy China. Faces are lifelike, nudging up just shy of the uncanny valley as close-ups reveal porous details, lip quivers, and more, bringing an excellent cast of Chinese performances to life. The English voice acting has its standouts, but Soul’s voice is boring, so I highly recommend the Chinese vocals.

Boss fights draw clear inspiration from Chinese cinema and boast a wondrous sense of awe and scale that only the best in the genre typically offer. There are a ton of bosses, too, with very few repeats (repeats do happen in segmented challenge trials), and it’s impressive to think back on just how many I defeated, and just how many of them delivered a unique fight. I appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases as well. There are so many bosses – nearing 100 or more if I had to guess – and having my progression saved through phases removes some of the repetition I often feel when, say, phase two of a boss continues to kill me and I have to blitz through phase one again and again before taking another stab at it.

That scale and on-screen excitement carry through almost every fight in the game, down to even the simplest mob fights, though these are starting to feel a touch repetitive as I’m barreling toward the game’s end. Soul moves like the world’s greatest martial artist, but your controller inputs make it happen. If you mash the attack button, it looks nice… but if you use each weapon’s prescribed inputs and abilities, Phantom Blade Zero delivers a level of detailed action I’ve seen in few other games. You direct the game’s action, and this lets you turn what might otherwise be just another group of fodder enemies into an electric bout of spectacle.

To say I greatly enjoy this game greatly undersells my feelings – writing this review-in-progress is frustrating because I want to get back to Phantom Blade Zero. I expect to reach credits in the coming days, so please be on the lookout for my final verdict this week.

#4278. Battlefield 6 kicks off its first free trial post the Black Ops 7 launch to twist that knife

Activision has done its own fair share of Battlefield 6 counterprogramming prior to that game's release, and EA is here to repay the favour with Black Ops 7.

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now launched, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

The recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was announced last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy launched, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

The trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

Players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this issue before the trial officially kicks off.

#4277. Infinity Nikki 2.0 launches with a whole new region, archery skills, and a new theme song by original Wicked actor Idina Menzel

Infinity Nikki's version 2.0 is the game's biggest evolution yet, transforming almost every part of it.

Infinity Nikki has officially evolved into a bigger, more feature-rich game. After months of waiting, version 2.0 has arrived to bring massive overhauls - and plenty of new content - to the dress-up RPG.

The update, available now on all platforms, is dubbed Terra’s Call. It adds a new region, Itzaland, to the game’s world. It also reshapes the rest of Miraland.

Itzaland is only the tip of the iceberg. Elderwood Forest and Spira are the region's two new areas, with more to be unlocked down the line. This patch also upgrades several core mechanics, including combat and exploration. There’s a suite of new traversal abilities, too, like grappling, low-gravity and even gigantification.

Archery is a new addition to combat, and you’ll spot new combat companions as part of the adaptive energy mechanics. Terra’s Call clearly has a focus on interactivity with the game’s world, to make it feel more alive and lived-in.

There’s a host of new interactions you can have with cute creatures like singing mushrooms, and wall-climbing snails. Version 2.0 also makes for a great starting point for new players as both main and side stories are now available for free.

It wouldn’t be a dress-up game without a host of new fashion sets, and outfits, of course - and there's plenty here, both free and paid. The launch of the new update also kicks off several in-game events, including some that celebrate the game’s second anniversary, and Nikki’s birthday.

Infold also recently announced that Idina Menzel — the actor who originated the roles of Elphaba in Wicked and Elsa in Frozen — will be singing the brand-new theme song for Version 2.0. You can listen to that on the official Infinity Nikki YouTube channel, where you can also watch a behind-the-scenes interview with Ms Menzel.

#4276. Report: Ghost Of Yōtei Developer Sucker Punch Hit With Layoffs

Sucker Punch, the team behind Ghost of Yōtei, Ghost of Tsushima, Infamous, and Sly Cooper, has been hit with layoffs, according to a report by Aftermath. The outlet states that 26 roles have been affected as the studio prepares its next project.

Aftermath cites a former Sucker Punch employee who confirmed the number of layoffs. The outlet also obtained a company email announcing the staff cuts.

“After carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project, we've decided to make some staffing reductions. Several positions across Sucker Punch will be eliminated as a result,” reads a section of the email. Sucker Punch then says it will work to support affected staff in their transition and will share more details next week about what comes next. The studio has not yet publicly commented on the layoffs.

This news comes a few weeks after the release of the Complete Edition of Ghost of Yōtei, which originally launched in 2025 to critical and commercial success. The release coincided with the arrival of two substantial DLCs: the story expansion Echoes of Sekigahara and a roguelike mode called Most Wanted that reintroduces Ghost of Tsushima hero Jin Sakai as a playable character.

#4275. The latest Arc Raiders patch is almost entirely about fixing exploits, including all the clipping through locked rooms business

Embark is clearly sick of Arc Raiders players exploiting the game's mechanics to push each other around, and clip through doors and walls.

A fresh Arc Raiders patch has arrived, bringing a host of new fixes to several exploits players have recently been relying on to do things they’re not supposed to, and bypass certain mechanics to get into areas without having to go through proper channels.

The patch is fairly small, and surprisingly doesn’t include any buffs or nerfs to anything in particular.

The list of notes for update 1.4.0 is compact, with a clear focus on addressing several exploits. The biggest one, of course, is the addition of “exploit mitigation mechanisms” to stop players from glitching through locked doors.

This fix applies to all maps, and it’s intended to address an issue whereby players would not bring the required keys to access those areas of the various maps. Locked rooms, if they can be unlocked, often hide a wealth of high-tier and rare loot.

But players have also been using similar exploits to clip through walls and access areas outside the playspace, allowing them to ambush enemy players and set up traps that would be impossible for others to detect.

The game’s recent patch, which was released exactly one week ago, mainly consisted of balance tweaks to some of the more popular weapons and mines. However, it also introduced a few fixes to prevent players from clipping through walls by using barricades.

While on the subject of being in places where you’re not supposed to, the patch blocked exterior access to the locked room inside Spaceport's Control Tower, making it only accessible from inside the tower.

#4274. Riftbound Champion Decks Revealed For Set Seven

While Riftbound set seven, The Reckoning, is still a long way off, we're steadily learning more about the set, including who will lead the Champion Decks.

Courtesy of The Riftbound Report, fans are ecstatic to see that Shyvana will lead one of the decks, while iconic ADC Vayne leads the other. Despite being a long-serving character in the game, Vayne has only one card in Riftbound so far: a Champion Unit from Origins, while this is Shyvana's debut in the TCG.

While details about the decks are minimal at this stage, we will run you through what we do know, as well as the other confirmed legends for The Reckoning, which is due for release in April 2027.

Given that The Reckoning isn't due to hit shelves until April 2027, we wouldn't expect to have too many details this early. However, The Riftbound Report is stating that the two Champions Decks are already confirmed, with Shyvana leading a Fury and Body rune deck, while Vayne will lead a Chaos and Order rune deck.

We don't yet have a closer look at the Legend cards for each character, nor any additional details about each deck. However, Champion Decks are expected to keep the same approach and follow the same structure as previous products. This means you can expect a 40-card main deck, a 12-card rune deck, a Legend card, and three battlefields. You also get one booster back for the associated set included in the box, a deck box, and a paper playmat.

The recommended MSRP for Champion Decks is $19.99, although this could change by the time Reckoning comes around.

Not including the four Proving Grounds decks, there have been seven solo Champion Decks released so far, and two Showdown sets, where each box features two decks.

Even League of Legends' own Riftbound isn't safe from the scalpers infesting the Trading Card Game community.

While very little is known about Riftbound set seven, mainly because we have a whole other set to get through first in 2027, we do have a list of five total Legends that have been confirmed so far:

There are four more Legends that are still to be announced at a later date. Riftbound doesn't quite follow the same rigid structure that games like Magic: The Gathering and Disney Lorcana follow with their set info drops, and this can mean that players feel like they're missing out on key information that half the fanbase knew ahead of time.

In time, it would be great for Riftbound to get its messaging completely under control, as this allows for a more organized approach to each new set, and players won't be left wondering which new cards, be they leaks or official releases, are coming in which sets.

#4273. Grammy Award-Winning Composer Austin Wintory Shares His Early Musical Drafts Intended For Mass Effect 5

Last week, EA shut down Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare, which resulted in the cancellation of the fifth Mass Effect game that was announced in 2020. As the fallout from this closure settles, famed video game composer Austin Wintory has shared that he'd been working on a potential soundtrack for the now-canceled game and has publicly released early versions of this score.

In a Bluesky thread, Wintory, who has composed soundtracks for games such as Journey, Sword of the Sea (for which he won a Grammy), Assassin’s Creed: Syndicate, and The Banner Saga trilogy, writes, “Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale, my all-time dream project. For the last couple years I'd been in discussion w/ BioWare & EA to take on the project & as part of that I wrote close to 20 minutes of music to explore where the franchise can go next, may as well share it!"

Wintory uploaded a 20-minute video consisting of eight tracks to his YouTube channel. The video begins with a message further elaborating on the partnership between BioWare, EA, and him. “For the past several years, I’d been in dialogue with people both at BioWare and EA to potentially jump into Mass Effect 5. As part of these conversations, I decided to surprise the team by writing/recording a gigantic love letter to the franchise, with my idea of where it can go next.”

Wintory adds that he composed the music in 2025 and that he “knew nothing” about what Mass Effect 5's story entailed when he did. As such, he describes the music as “narratively speculative.” He adds that this conceptual soundtrack was a direct homage to Jack Wall and Sam Hulick’s soundtrack on the first Mass Effect “while leaning even harder on true analog synths, and a more complex integration of the orchestra (almost akin to the hybrid nature of The Matrix),” he writes. Each music track features a message by Wintory explaining his inspiration for its production.

“Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss," Wintory writes in the video's description. "It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever. Thank you nonetheless to everyone at BioWare and EA's music department for gifting me the chance to dream in your sandbox. It was a privilege to do even that much.”

Wintory's music is the latest piece of potential Mass Effect 5 content to emerge since BioWare’s closure. A day after the shutdown announcement, an unreleased but reportedly legitimate cinematic trailer for the canceled Mass Effect leaked online.

#4271. Battlefield Labs is coming back for a short session to test out next week's Battlefield 6 update, and you can expect more tests in the future, too

Battlefield Labs is evolving, as it reopens its doors for its next - unusual - session.

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season update not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

The December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the new year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

Battlefield Studios announced a host of new changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

The focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an issue that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

The patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios says should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

Going forward, Battlefield Studios said to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

Some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect new maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

#4270. Free-To-Play MOBA Pokémon Unite Is Shutting Down In March

The free-to-play MOBA Pokémon Unite will shut down in March, over five years after its 2021 launch. Although a gradual suspension of services begins today, fans will enjoy one last hurrah thanks to a big in-game event running for the remainder of the game’s lifecycle.

Launched in July 2021 for Switch before migrating to iOS and Android later that year, Pokémon Unite was billed as a friendlier take on the MOBA genre popularized by Dota 2 and League of Legends, thanks to its short matches (10 minutes) and simplified mechanics. Despite its initial popularity, the game is winding down and will go offline for good on March 23, 2027.

An End of Service notice on the game’s website reads,

“We offer our sincerest gratitude to the many Trainers who have played since service started for the Nintendo Switch version on July 21, 2021. We would like to express our thanks to everyone by holding a special event until service ends. The Pokémon Unite Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo competitive tournament (an event for Pokémon Unite only) will also be held as previously announced. We hope you continue to enjoy Pokémon Unite until the final day of service. After service ends, the 'Pokémon Unite Game Content Guidelines for Online Platforms' will no longer be published or maintained, and we will no longer provide support regarding use of Pokémon Unite videos and images.”

As of today, in-game sales of Aeos gems and Unite Club memberships/renewals have been suspended. Existing Unite Club members will continue to use their benefits until the end of the membership period.

On November 12, an update will kick off the aforementioned final special event, where players can obtain items such as all Unite licenses and Holoware that have appeared in the game up to that point. A library feature will also be added, letting players view certain records and in-game content even after the game shuts down on March 23. Those who don’t download the library feature before the shutdown date will not be able to get it afterward.

Qualifiers for the Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo Competitive tournament will take place as planned on December 5. After the game shuts down on March 23, players won't be able to log in to Pokémon Unite or play any battles. Only the library feature will remain accessible.

We enjoyed Pokémon Unite when it launched, with executive video editor Alex Van Aken scoring it an 8 out of 10 in his review, writing, “The game eats away the hours of my day as I reassuringly say to myself, 'Just one more match.' Battles play out with the spectacle that the Pokémon series is known for, and with so many abilities to choose from, no match feels the same as the last. The game’s simple mechanics and recognizable characters make for an approachable MOBA experience, and with a potential catalog of nearly 900 Pokémon to pick from, my hopes are high for the future of Pokémon Unite.”

#4268. French Union Accuses Microsoft of Deadlocking Marvel’s Blade

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

Many studios have been in rough patches recently, either due to internal struggles amid the modern challenges of development or due to layoffs or closures mandated by larger owners. It's easy to write off every issue in the modern industry as someone else’s fault, but that’s not realistic; every part of the industry is struggling, inside and out.

The upcoming God of War spin-off has been delayed to May 20th, dodging the busy February release window.

Arkane Lyon is one studio that's been in hot water for a long while, struggling to find a buyer before Microsoft closes its doors. Following hopeful news as more buyers step up, a French union with ties to Arkane staff has accused Microsoft of attempting to sabotage the development of the studio’s current project, Blade, by barring hires for over a year.

The development of Marvel’s Blade has been absolutely hectic, between internal shifts in the game’s vision and an early announcement that put heat on Arkane far before they were ready. Now, STJV, the French union representing certain members of Arkane Lyon’s staff, has made a major accusation, claiming the game is coming along fine, despite Microsoft’s interference.

According to STJV in a direct quotation, “Today, as work on Blade is going fine, and the level of quality of the game to be expected is on [par] with what Arkane has accustomed its players, workers have to face the harsh reality: our studio might get closed because, and only because, Microsoft decided to, even if that means sabotaging the game it funded.”

This all still has yet to be confirmed, as no direct response from Microsoft has been released, despite the accusations levied by STJV. Alongside the biting remarks, the union has dropped a series of demands, including a say in who buys Arkane, and a larger payout for the staff if no buyer steps forward.

It's easy to write off every issue in the modern industry as someone else’s fault, but that’s not realistic, every part of the industry is struggling, inside and out.

Despite all of this swinging out, Arkane is still eager to release Blade, staying optimistic that the title will release in the following years if Arkane is allowed to keep their doors open. STJV keeps the argument practical, framing the studio’s progress as a financial incentive for both parties. “Even this closure itself is done against any financial logic, as closing Arkane today would probably be more expensive than finishing the game,” says STJV.

Arkane’s aim to finish the game despite their wild situation is comforting to see, and gives me real hope at the quality of their Blade title, as long as it manages to release. The whispers of big studios like Ubisoft’s interest make it clear more than just Arkane want to see the title released, and as the months continue to tick by with the company still open, those whispers just get louder.

Arkane is a studio that would feel like a serious loss for the larger gaming industry if they closed their doors, even after stumbles like Redfall. Dropping into the mainstream scene with hits like Dishonored and Prey, Arkane Lyon is infamous for worlds that feel so lived-in, even after devastation has raked across them.

They truly do feel like the perfect team to work on Blade, as their mastery of immersive sims and wild powers leaves massive room for the exact type of action Blade is perfect for. It really does feel like every production surrounding Blade is hexed, if the canceled films and Arkane’s own pains are anything to look at.

I’m very eager to hear a response from Microsoft, as STJV has levied some major accusations that could really disrupt how third parties and internal studios interact with them. At present, we only have STJV’s word to go off of, so take these accusations with a grain of salt until more comes out.

#4267. Honkai: Star Rail 3.8 will run for an extra two weeks while Version 4.0 is in the oven

The next Honkai: Star Rail update is upon us, and there's a mix of good - and unusual news.

HoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major update. Version 3.8 was the big highlight, of course, with the new release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

Alongside showing everything coming with this next update, the developer also announced that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

This final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

The new playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

The Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

While The Dahlia is the only new character appearing in this final Amphoreus update, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the new patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.
