#4266. Overwatch Isn't Slowing Down After Its 10th Anniversary

I spoke with Overwatch game director Aaron Keller and associate game director Alec Dawson about the game's future.

If 2026 had a defining trait for Overwatch, it was ambition. Celebrating its 10th anniversary, Blizzard's hero shooter went bigger than ever, dropping five new heroes at the start of the year and introducing a year-long narrative with The Reign of Talon. With Season 5 bringing that story to a close, it's fascinating to think how Blizzard can possibly top itself.

The good news is, the team isn't particularly interested in playing it safe. During a recent group interview I attended with game director Aaron Keller and associate game director Alec Dawson, I got a glimpse of what the next chapter looks like. While the developers aren't ready to spill all their secrets ahead of February's Overwatch Spotlight, there's already a clear message: 2027 won't simply be a repeat of 2026.

"We don't want players to feel like there is this tight playbook that we're following every year," Keller says. The team still wants to deliver a major annual release, but keeping players guessing is part of the appeal. "Yes, every year we do want to release something big," he says, teasing a February expansion that has been in development for quite some time.

Overwatch has spent the past two years focusing on Perks, Stadium, new heroes, and a renewed attention to storytelling. Though there's a difference between maintaining that momentum and making every update that follows an increasingly cool spectacle.

For Dawson, the answer is knowing when to add something new and when to take a step back. "We're curators and also caretakers at the same time," he says. The team wants to introduce new experiences, but it's equally important to make sure existing systems are healthy. That means paying attention to progression, balance, and the smaller improvements that might not generate a Twitter-breaking announcement, but make a difference to the people logging in every day.

Perhaps the biggest change this year has been seeing Overwatch commit to a continuous narrative again. The Reign of Talon gave us an entire year to follow Vendetta's rise, Doomfist's downfall, and the shifting relationships between the game's growing cast of heroes. Best of all, Blizzard has no intention of putting the comics away just yet.

"I'm so excited for the 2027 story that's going to be coming out," Keller says. In fact, he believes the next opening cinematic could be the best the team has ever produced.

The upcoming Season 6 hero trailer will also serve as the prologue to that next narrative, which will lay the groundwork for what's coming. Keller says the team is investing even more in storytelling next year, although there's some room for improvement in how it delivers that content.

One problem is that Overwatch's story can be easy to miss. From cinematics, motion comics, smaller character-focused stories, and Webtoon releases, keeping up can sometimes feel like a chore. Even players who enjoy the lore might not know where to look for the next piece.

Keller acknowledges that the team needs to make its narrative more accessible, while Dawson wants individual story arcs to feel more connected to the world around them. It's not enough for one storyline to end and another to begin; the events in between should have consequences.

That's exciting for longtime fans who have spent years waiting for certain character relationships and unfinished storylines to receive some attention. Keller even hints that 2027's narrative will revisit previously established material rather than starting completely from scratch.

For all the new heroes, narrative developments, and experimental modes, Keller and Dawson are conscious that Overwatch can't simply keep adding things forever. With 2026 adding an unprecedented number of new characters, the team is already thinking about how to keep the experience readable and welcoming to newcomers.

"We're not there yet," Keller says of the point where the roster might become too large to sustain the current release pace. Still, it's something the developers discuss internally.

That's the most interesting takeaway from our conversation. Blizzard isn't treating Overwatch's 10th anniversary as an excuse to coast on nostalgia. It wants to keep experimenting, but it also seems increasingly aware that the game's future depends on knowing which experiments are worth keeping.

The next Overwatch Spotlight will come in February 2027, and there are promises of another huge expansion. Keller isn't ready to reveal exactly what's coming, but he is making one thing super clear: Team 4 wants to surprise players rather than just continue to follow last year's formula.

After a decade of reinventions, cancellations, comebacks, and more than a few community arguments, Overwatch is heading into its next chapter with plenty left to prove. Fortunately, it sounds like Blizzard isn't running out of ideas just yet.

#4264. Tomorrow’s Battlefield 6 patch is the first step towards improving footstep audio, and it might actually fix the settings reset bug

The next major Battlefield 6 patch is nearly upon us, and Battlefield Studios is promising a bounty of changes - including a couple of fixes to some big bugs.

Battlefield 6 is about to receive a new update. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only new weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Easily the most interesting change in this update is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a big pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this update is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an update. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the issue should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

#4263. Phantom Blade Zero Review – Wuxia Wonder Abounds

Rooted in Wuxian storytelling and scale, built on an impressively detailed combat system, and wrapped in a bloody Chinese martial underground that’s a genuine joy to play in, Phantom Blade Zero is a feat. It joins an echelon of action pedigree that includes Sekiro, Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and just about any other action game you hold in high regard. It hails from developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile and smaller-scale games, and I’m shocked by what it’s pulled off with its triple-A action inauguration. But make no mistake: though Phantom Blade Zero is this team’s first crack at a game like this, it is an incredibly confident, strong debut.

Protagonist Soul is a stoic martial arts master betrayed by the Order he’s sworn his life to; he dies and returns to life with only 66 days to live. That’s enough time to settle his debts, repay his betrayers, and end a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the Wulin realm. This narrative is Phantom Blade Zero's weakest link, but its premise adds enough mystery and tension to keep this Wuxian journey exciting through to its final, realm-shattering moments. Narrative bombshells drop not just through the game’s general fantasy-realism art direction, but also through anime scenes, opera puppet shows, animated brushstroke sequences, and more, highlighting Chinese culture and its integral place in Phantom Blade Zero.

The game features a staggering number of unique enemy types, and though the final hours get a bit repetitive, it’s admirable how long S-Game maintains such a high level of combat-oriented ecstasy. Soul’s access to weapons drives that exhilaration. Every weapon is wholly unique. Because the combat is combo-based, picking up a new weapon feels like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. Each has its own moveset and abilities, with later-game weapons featuring combo lists that look more at home in a Street Fighter menu. Add in the special, tide-turning weapons known as Phantom Edges, with limited charge-based uses, and there’s no shortage of permutations to delightfully experiment with.

Drawing on Chinese cinema, Phantom Blade Zero's setpiece bosses boast a sense of awe and scale only the genre's best typically offer. With virtually no repeat bosses, save for a few in separate trials, it’s impressive how many powerful figures I flayed, and how many delivered a unique fight. I also appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases, as they remove the frustrating repetition of replaying phase one again and again just to take another stab at the second phase I’m struggling with.

You’d be forgiven for assuming Phantom Blade Zero is a Soulslike, given its challenging bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, this game’s equivalent of bonfires. It definitively isn’t, though. The challenge is much more surmountable; the game isn’t interested in making you die over and over, there are difficulty options, and you can equip accessories to make parries and dodges easier. World progression is materially different, too, as enemies don’t respawn after you kill them. It’s an interesting, perhaps blasphemous, choice for the genre, but it's surprisingly effective, adding a sense of worldbuilding and tangible progression I didn’t know I wanted from my action games. Soul is on a mission to remove evil, and mechanically, I’m doing just that. Enemies don’t respawn incoherently just because I heal and save.

Environmental features weave in and out of each other, and the architectural design and layout of these regions lead to many subsequent “aha” moments. S-Game infuses search-action elements into this exploration through the aforementioned Phantom Edges, some of which double as tools to unlock surprising new areas in both new and previously visited biomes. As a result, backtracking and exploration remain fresh. A lot of it is optional, as are some of Phantom Blade Zero's most rewarding elements, including its demanding “perfect” ending. Sadly, this renders other endings unsatisfying, with clear chunks intentionally missing.

Despite forays into the Uncanny Valley, Phantom Blade Zero is visually striking, and the action is brilliantly animated. It’s all set to genre-breaking music, too, with original metalcore songs, operatic choirs, 808s, and traditional Chinese instrumentation, creating a score as illustrious as the action it enhances.

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding action achievement, almost unbelievably so for a game that is essentially a studio’s genre debut. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, one that recognizes the genre’s strengths and weaknesses and addresses both with fantastical Wuxian style. Though the action genre is always jam-packed with new releases, few are as special as Phantom Blade Zero.

#4261. Where Winds Meet December's calendar is full of new content, including a new region and the mobile launch you've been waiting for

You're probably nowhere near done with what's already in Where Winds Meet, but you better believe there's more on the way.

Where Winds Meet already has a staggering amount of content, but that’s not the end of what we can expect. Developer Everstone Studio just revealed a host of new additions coming to the game this month.

It’s clear that the developer is committed to the free-to-play action RPG, and the game’s recent success on Steam, and PlayStation has more than likely solidified the team’s plans for the future of the game.

On the official Where Winds Meet account on Twitter, the developer shared a brief roadmap of some of what we can expect over the course of December. The roadmap is split into the four weeks of the month, covering everything from smaller quests to more larger additions.

The first week started off a little light, with two new Jianghu Legacy Quests: Twelve Years of Feuds, and An Unholy Prophecy. Both quests are currently available in the game.

The biggest addition, of course, is the new Roarding Sands region, which becomes available the same day as the RPG’s global launch on mobile devices during the second week. Roarding Sands arrives December 11, along with a new campaign boss dubbed River Master.

Discover the Winds of December:🗺️New Region: Roaring Sands🌊New Bosses: River Master and Feng Ruzhi📱Global Mobile Launch: Dec 12 (UTC)🗡️New Hero's Realm, Sword Trial and more! pic.twitter.com/d12Ra9uXwb

We also expect a new boss, Feng Ruzhi, to be added to the game during the same week, as well as the arrival of the Velvet Shade Sect. Two limited-time activities kick off during the same week, too; The Fortune Beyond Parlor, and The Great Faceologist.

The third and fourth weeks of the month bring us the Scarlet Shock Sword Trial, as well as the new Blazing Gale Dance Hero’s Realm activity. Where Winds meet wraps it all up on December 30 with the Fireworks Festival.

If you just got started in this massive RPG, we have a host of incredibly useful Where Winds Meet guides. Some of the most common questions have been how to join the Silver Needle sect, how to to get Celestial Seize, where to find and unlock Mystic Arts.

The answers to those, and many more, are yours at the link. We recently updated our codes page with new codes, too, so definitely check that out for some in-game freebies.

#4260. Battlefield 6's latest update dubbed the game's simultaneously best and worst patch as it runs into all kinds of issues

What's likely going to be the last major Battlefield 6 update of the year has launched with a number of unexpected issues.

There’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some new holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the update’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.

Immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The issue is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios quickly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The issue remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer said it’s working on a proper fix.

Perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

Ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to quickly jump into the new content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the issue, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the update.

But Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an update once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the new Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

This is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the new update has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

It’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many issues at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.

#4258. Where To Find All Pieces Of Heart In The Ocarina Of Time Remake

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake boasts quite a few collectibles to find throughout Hyrule. From Gold Skulltula to bag upgrades to three different elemental arrows, these can all help you make your life a little easier when facing off against the forces of Ganondorf.

Perhaps the most important item to find is the 36 Pieces of Heart, which will raise Link's overall health, making him much harder to put down. However, many of these aren't easily found and will require a bit of legwork. Additionally, several of these will be in brand new locations, so even if you're an Ocarina of Time veteran, you won't always be able to rely on your past experiences.

Here is where to find all the Pieces of Heart in the Ocarina of Time remake.

Some quick information before we get to the actual locations. The first thing is this list will not cover the full Heart Containers you get after defeating every major boss. They are basically unmissable and act as rewards for finishing a dungeon. Additionally, this list will be in chronological order, meaning, this is the order you can unlock them as you play the game.

Because of this, I recommend bookmarking this guide and using it as a reference for when you play. That way, as you progress through the story, you can grab every Piece of Heart available in that moment.

Your first Piece of Heart can be found at Lon Lon Ranch in the middle of Hyrule Field. When you arrive at the ranch, head to the back right corner where the large, partially destroyed stone tower is. Inside, there will be several crates you need to move, so shift them around so the middle one and one on the left that are closest to the metal bars are pulled away. This lets you crawl into the hole and reach the Heart Piece on the other side of the tunnel.

Kakariko Graveyard (Night) — Dampe's Graveyard Mini-Game

In the graveyard at night, talk to Dampe while he is roaming around to play the Graveyard Tour game. For this, you will need to pay him 10 Rupees to dig out one of eleven possible spots around the graveyard. Unfortunately, the Piece of Heart is entirely randomized, so you cannot reliably always pick the same location. Thankfully, you can always save, pick a spot, and if it's not right, reload the save and try again. You're looking for a dig spot that is hardened, requiring you to pay Dampe a second time. Sadly, this also isn't always a guarantee, but it's what you're looking for.

Kakariko Graveyard (Night) — Under The Tombstone

Staying in the graveyard, you can find the next Heart Piece by moving the farthest tombstone on the right in the second row all the way back. This will reveal a hole you can jump down into where you'll find a big chest with a Heart Piece inside.

You can get this Piece of Heart once you've obtained the Fairy Ocarina, but it's easier to just get it once you've been tasked with learning Saria's Song. Upon entering the Lost Woods via the Kokiri Forest entrance, hang a right to enter an area with a target hanging from a tree. Go down the ladder to the lower level and step onto the tree stump in front of the two Skull Kids. You will now need to complete three games of Simon Says, where you repeat on your ocarina what they play on their flutes.

The next Piece of Heart in the Lost Woods can be obtained right after you get Saria's Song. Once you have learned this tune, from the Kokiri Forest entrance, go left through the large hole to the left to find a long Skull Kid sitting on a tree in front of an empty tree stump. Climb onto the tree stump, take out your Fairy Ocarina, and play Saria's Song.

Your next Heart Piece can be acquired after you've received the Goron Bracelet from Darunia. Now that you can pick up Bomb Flowers, take out your Deku Stick and use it to light the torches around the massive vase at the bottom floor of the city. This will cause the vase to start spinning around on its platform. Now go to the next floor and grab the Bomb Flow in the back left corner by the mural of dancing Gorons (circled in the photo). Quickly run over to the edge and throw the Bomb Flower into the top of the vase. If you can get the Bomb Flower to explode while inside the vase, it will spit out a Piece of Heart.

Death Mountain Crater — Near The Entrance

Obtainable after you've beaten Dodongo's Cavern, this Piece of Heart is located at the very top of Death Mountain. Head up the mountain, and when you reach the massive opening, make sure you are at full health before heading inside. You'll have a very short time before you burn to death, so the moment you enter, sprint for the netting hanging over the edge of the cliffs on the left. Climb down the netting, and at the bottom will be the Heart Piece. This will fully restore your health, so quickly climb back up and run out!

One of the easiest in the game to miss, this Piece of Heart can only be found as Young Link in Death Mountain Crater. From the entrance, head left and down to the lower level that's to the right of the bombable hole in the ground. There you will find a Business Scrub who attacks when you're near. Use a Deku Nut to stun him and then hit him once. He will apologize for being so aggressive and will sell you a Piece of Heart for 100 Rupees. Again, remember that this can only be done as Young Link, which means you'll be taking damage this whole time so move fast!

You can get the next Piece of Heart immediately after obtaining the one in Death Mountain Crater. Upon exiting the crater, talk to the large owl, Kaepora, and ask him to bring you to the base of the mountain. After a brief cutscene, he will drop you off on a roof in Kakoriko Village. Go to the back left corner of the roof and look down at the stables. There will be a Piece of Heart on the red roof you can jump to!

Hyrule Castle Town — Bombchu Bowling Alley

Now that we have Bombs, the Bombchu Bowling Alley has officially opened in Hyrule Castle Town. When you arrive in town, go to the square and enter the parlor on the left. Talk to the vendor to play the game, which requires you to destroy three yellow targets with the Bombchus you're supplied. There are three difficulty levels to this mini-game, and you'll need to beat all of them to unlock the Piece of Heart. This is pretty easy, as you don't have a time limit and will have way more bombs than you need. Don't be afraid to destroy the obstacles, as this will use a bomb, but it makes hitting any target behind it way easier!

You can get another Piece of Heart in town, but you can only do it at night. Once the sun is down, look for the larger woman crying by the town entrance. Speak to her to learn that her dog, Richard, has run off, and she wants you to find it. You'll notice there are a ton of stray dogs running around town, so this seems like a difficult task. Thankfully, we know that Richard is colored white, which heavily limits which dog he is. Go down the alley on the left and interact with the first white dog you find to make it follow you. Bring this back to the woman to learn if it's Richard or not. If it is, you'll get a Piece of Heart; if not, you'll need to go find a different white dog. This is very much trial and error, so it may take a few attempts until you bring over the correct dog.

With our business concluded in Castle Town, make your way to Gerudo Valley, which is to the west in Hyrule Fields. When you arrive, grab the Cucco then walk to the left of the suspension bridge. You will see a chest on a cliff across the gap below you. While holding the Cucco, jump off and use it to float across the ravine. Drop the chicken near the chest and open it to get a Piece of Heart!

Gerudo Valley — Gerudo Valley Entrance Waterfall

Staying in Gerudo Valley, take the Cucco and take it back to where the suspension bridge is. Jump off the cliff while holding the bird and float down towards the massive waterfall on the right. When you land in the water, climb onto the nearby path and then head towards the waterfall. You will find a series of stone stairs behind this waterfall that leads to a small opening where the Piece of Heart can be found.

For this Piece of Heart, you need to catch a fish that is 58cm or bigger at the Fishing Pond. Found on the west side of Lake Hylia. Talk to the owner of the Fishing Pond about renting a fishing rod, and then try to cast your lure near the center of the watering hole. You're specifically looking for a large green fish, as that's the one I caught that earned me the Piece of Heart. This may take a few attempts, but there's no time limit, and you can use the fishing rod as much as you want once it has been rented. Just keep aiming for the bigger, bright green fish, and you'll snag one that's the right size. Once you do, return to the vendor and give him your fish to earn your prize.

The first Piece of Heart in Zora's River can be found roughly halfway up the river. When you arrive, progress upstream until you can go behind the locked gate where the Magic Bean Salesman is sitting in front of you. Behind it will be a Cucco, so grab that and carry it up the river until you reach an area with two Blue Tektites. Throw the bird onto the path in front, kill the bugs, and then pick it back up. Now, don't go upstream anymore; instead use the Cucco to fly across the gap to the south. Release the bird, climb the vines, and then head to the small area you need to reach via a small jump to the south. There you'll find a hole; go into the hole, grab the Cucco, and return to the surface. Finally, use that Cucco to reach the Piece of Heart on the elevated rocky platform.

The next Piece of Heart is close by and doesn't require nearly as much work. This time, take a Cucco all the way to the end of the river. On the north side, at the start of the river, you will see a small cliff where the Heart Piece resides. Use the Cucco to jump and cross the gap to obtain this upgrade.

The only Piece of Heart in Zora Domain is obtained by lighting all the unlit torches in the area. You start at the top where King Zora is and will work your way down the stairs and under the waterfall where you practice diving and earn the Silver Scale item. Once all the torches are lit, a large chest will appear with the Heart Piece inside.

This Piece of Heart can be found in the Kakariko Graveyard on the left. Assuming you planted a Magic Bean into the Bug Hole on the left, you can now find a large flower that Link can ride in the future. Step onto the flower, let it raise you up to the ruins and grab the Piece of Heart on the pedestal.

After beating Dampe in a race and unlocking the Hookshot, follow the path up the ruined stairs. Use the Hookshot to cross the gap, which will spit you out in Kakariko Village's windmill. Now carefully walk onto the rotating platform and ride it over to the next Heart Piece.

The next Piece of Heart can be acquired by completing Dampe's Race a second time and reaching the finish line in under a minute. This isn't as difficult as it sounds thanks to the new sprint button. The trick here is to never stop running, cut as many corners as you can, and do not get hit once by his fire. Getting struck by his flames can end your entire attempt, so always stick towards the walls, as Dampe rarely throws his flames right next to them. Also, you may run past a ReDead, but do not stop or even give it a chance to stun you! Beat Dampe in under a minute and the Piece of Heart is yours.

Now that we have the Hookshot, we can get onto the roof of the Potion Shop and talk to the man on it. Go up toward the gate to Death Mountain Trail and enter the Potion Shop on the right. Use the back door behind the counter to the left and then look to the other Potion Shop's roof on the right. Aim the Hookshot at the vines to pull you onto the roof. Talk to the man sitting there to earn a Heart Piece.

Back at Lake Hylia, if you planted a Magic Bean, you can step onto the large flower right next to the Lakeside Laboratory entrance. Ride the flower around Lake Hylia and jump off when it reaches the top of the Laboratory. Climb up the tower to find a Piece of Heart at the top.

Lake Hylia — Lakeside Laboratory Interior

To get this Piece of Heart you will need to get the Golden Scale. This is done by first beating the fish record as Young Link to earn a Piece of Heart and then doing it a second time as Adult Link. Remember, to reach the Fishing Pond in the future, you need to ride the Magic Bean Flower and jump off when it passes by. Once you have the Golden Scale, go into the laboratory, jump into the dive tank, and swim all the way to the bottom. Touch the floor underwater, then return to the surface. The Lake Scientist will be impressed with your skills and give you a Piece of Heart.

Your next Gold Skulltula is located in the Skulltula House. Once you've collected 50 Gold Skulltulas, you can visit this location in Kakariko Village and talk to them to earn a Piece of Heart. This only works if you get 50 Gold Skultulas, so make sure to use our guide if you are missing some!

Go back in the past once you learn the Song of Storms and at least five other songs. Once you have enough tunes, go to Zora River and look for the five colored frogs along the northern wall about halfway through this area. Play five different songs, not including the Song of Storms, to cause them all to grow. After making them grow, play the Song of Storms to cause it to rain earning you a Piece of Heart.

Stay at the frogs and listen as they offer to play a mini-game with you. You will need to play specific notes on your ocarina to make the frog with the spotlight on them jump up to catch the butterfly above them. Every frog has a corresponding button on your controller. Light Blue is L, Yellow is R, Dark Blue is Y, Grey is X, and Red is A. Complete the full mini-game with no mistakes to earn a Piece of Heart.

If you planted a Magic Bean in the soft soil spot right outside of Dodongo's Cavern, you will find a Magic Bean Flower. Step onto the flower to ride it up to the opening in the mountain directly above the dungeon entrance. There you will find your next Piece of Heart.

Death Mountain Crater — Magic Bean Flower

For this Piece of Heart, progress through the story until you learn the Bolero of Fire from Shiek. Once this happens, warp back to the Temple of Time and swap to young Link. Now, get a Magic Bean and a bug in a bottle. Play the Bolero of Fire and teleport there as a kid. You won't have much time, so quickly look for the bug hole right by the warp point. Use the bug to coax out a Gold Skulltula, kill it, then plant a Magic Bean in the soil. Teleport back to the Temple of Time, switch to adult Link, then finally return to the Fire Temple entrance. Step on the Magic Bean Flower and ride it to the next Piece of Heart.

This one is a little weird to get. First go towards Gerudo Valley in the west and head underneath the large stone arch on the right. Underneath, you will find an open chest, along with a Fairy Note on the wall. Read the note to learn that they unlocked the chest, but someone stole the Piece of Heart. Now, return to the past and visit this exact same spot as young Link. This time, you will find the chest unlocked, but still closed. Open the chest to get your Heart Piece.

Hyrule Field — Outside Hyrule Castle Town

I'm putting this here solely because my dumbass missed it and only discovered it a bit later. There's a chance you can absolutely get this as early as gaining the ability to go back and forth between time. To the right of the drawbridge outside of Hyrule Castle Town, along the stone wall, you will find a bombable patch of land. Going down the hole, you'll find a Business Scrub who will only sell items if you know the password. Go back up and look for a tree nearby that has a Fairy Thought carved into it. Reading it you will learn that the password is "Sell somethin', will ya?" Unfortunately, the future Business Scrub has already sold his Piece of Heart. Go back in time and return to this Business Scrub as young Link. Talk to him again and give the vendor the right password. You can now buy the Piece of Heart for 100 Rupees.

When you arrive at Zora Fountain as adult Link, you will find that Lord Jabu-Jabu is gone and there is ice everywhere. In the northeast corner of this area there will be several icy platforms that you can jump across to reach a Piece of Heart at the end. Just be careful, as there are Octoroks ready to attack along the path. Take your time crossing, and you'll easily snag this Heart Piece.

After completing the Ice Cavern, take some Blue Fire to King Zora to thaw him out of the ice. He will give you the Zora Tunic, allowing you to breathe underwater. Return to Zora Fountain and use the Iron Boots in combination with your new threads to sink to the bottom where the Piece of Heart is surrounded by a ring of Rupees.

Hyrule Castle Town — Treasure Chest Mini-Game

Once you unlock the Leneses of Truth, return to Hyrule Castle Town and head to the east. Look for the shop with the giant treasure chest above the door. Go inside and agree to play the mini-game. In each room, there will be two treasure chests, one of which has a Small Key inside. Use the Leneses to figure out which chest has the key, allowing you to progress to the next room. Do this five times, and the Piece of Heart is yours.

The next Piece of Heart is located at Gerudo Fortress. After you've gained the Gerudo Pass and can freely explore the fortress, make your way to the back rooftops. Go east along the roof until you reach a gap that's too large to jump. Play the Scarecrow Song to summon him across the gap, and then use the Longshot to pull yourself across. Inside the chest will be a Piece of Heart.

It's time to put those archery skills to the ultimate test. For this Piece of Heart, after you earned the Gerudo Pass, go to the southeastern corner of Gerudo Fortress. Summon Epona and talk to the woman under the awning. She will explain that they have a mini-game to see how many points you can earn. Your goal is to get 1,000 points in a single run. The simpletest way to do this is to hit 10 bullseyes (red circles), as these reward 100 points each. Once you get over 1,000 points, you'll get this Piece of Heart.

Our last Piece of Heart can be found in the Evil Desert Colossus. After you learn the Requiem of Spirit from Sheik, return to the Temple of Time and become Young Link. Then play the song to return to the Spirit Temple exterior. Right outside the door to the left, will be a bug hole you can plant a Magic Bean into. Once you do, come back to this location as Adult Link and ride the Magic Bean Flower through the area until it stops right in front of a Piece of Heart.

Nintendo has only gone and done it again.

#4257. Arc Raiders gets a few map exploit fixes in latest patch as Embark prepares to slow down how often patches are released

There's a new Arc Raiders patch that's fairly small, but one with fixes everyone is going to appreciate.

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

#4256. Nintendo Indie World Showcase Recap: Everything We Saw

The year is nearing its conclusion, and the last big AAA titles are rolling out one-by-one. But today, it was all about the independent titles on Nintendo's latest Indie World Showcase, highlighting new games from smaller indie teams coming to the Switch and Switch 2.

Here's everything we saw at the October 2026 Nintendo Indie World Showcase.

Today's Indie World Showcase started with a big headliner, as the long-awaited witch-life simulator Witchbrook got a release date. Chucklefish and Robtality's cozy magical world goes live on January 28, 2027.

Fans of 3D platformers should probably keep an eye on Winds of Viridia, which looks like a colorful game with a lot of interesting movement and exploration. Shark Jump's fantastical platformer is arriving next year, but if the wait's too long, a free demo is coming today on the eShop.

From one of the co-creators of Celeste, City of None has a gorgeous pixelated art style and colors that immediately remind me of Game Boy Color classics. It's a 2D platformer where you leap around, fight enemies, and explore the strange city around you. The jumping and fighting look solid, and I really like the mysterious atmosphere and art direction. City of None's set for sometime in 2027.

The sword-surfing adventure from the makers of Abzu and Journey is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on October 29, 2026 - tomorrow! It's a gorgeous adventure that earned a Must-Play badge from us, so it's worth your time if you like the kinds of gorgeous, beautiful adventures Giant Squid (developer of Abzu) is known for.

Take an overhead camera angle, brawler gameplay, and some John Wick sensibilities, and you've got Tenjutsu, a stylish roguelike where you use your martial arts prowess to tear apart crime syndicates. I really enjoy the look and vibe of this one, and it's from one of the designers of Dead Cells, too. Tenjutsu might be one to keep an eye on when it arrives on Switch 2 in 2027.

RPG fans have been eating well, and it looks like the feast could continue next year with Threads of Time. The time-traveling RPG is coming to both Switch and Switch 2 next summer, and it's looking absolutely gorgeous.

Ah, raccoons. Nature's most adorable little scamps. If you and your friends have ever wanted to live out the dream of being a rambunctious band of raccoons wreaking havoc on the town, Dumpster Gang sets out to give you just that fantasy in March 2027.

I've already enjoyed quite a bit of Super Battle Golf on PC, so I'll tell you now: if you enjoy golf games and want some Mario Party annoy-your-friends antics wound around them, Super Battle Golf should be on your radar for its March 25, 2027 launch on Switch 2.

Another port of a PC multiplayer mainstay, the co-op physics-driven horror-looter R.E.P.O. is coming to Switch 2 in 2027. This is one for the crowd that likes to be scared one moment and laughing hysterically the next.

Rounding out the co-op section, Haunted Paws has you and a pal playing as a pair of pups searching for their person in a haunted mansion. The side-scrolling 3D look makes it seem like a less-scary Little Nightmares, and the concept is pretty fun. Look for this one on Switch and Switch 2 in May 2027, or try out the free demo later today.

Enjoy shrines, towns, and strange night-time journeys into the unknown? Follow a fox girl and her frog friend on an adventure through a strange island in Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino on Switch 2 and Switch in spring 2027. I've said it a few times in this recap, but wow, the art here is great.

The second entry in the slime-collecting, home-building sim adventure is coming to Switch 2. Pick up adorable slimes with your vacuum, build a home for them, and explore the Rainbow Island around you in January 2027. Plus, there's an exclusive in-game item for the Switch 2 version.

From the makers of Cozy Grove, this multiplayer game encourages players to build a home above the clouds with friends and explore the world around them. Spirit Crossing looks like a big world to make your own alongside your pals, starting November 16, 2026 on both Switch and Switch 2.

Want something a little sillier? My Arms Are Longer Now is a game about, well, really long arms. With numerous Australian comedians lending their vocal talents to the project, this seems like it could be a quirky, charming, and delightfully funny experience when it arrives on both Switch and Switch 2 on March 11, 2027.

The delightfully Game Boy-styled critter delivery game Petal Runner is aiming for a full launch. I've played a bit of this one at events over the years, and it's charmed me every time. If you like nostalgic adventures with a surprisingly heartfelt core, you should mark down the March 8, 2027 launch, or check out the free demo arriving later today.

The chaotic coin-pushing game Raccoin is coming to Nintendo Switch 2. It's just like those token-shoving games you remember from arcades but with a number of wild and wacky means of pushing even more coins over the edge run-over-run. Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition hits Switch 2 on November 10, 2026, and a free demo is out later today.

#4255. Zenless Zone Zero shows off Ye Shunguang gameplay for the first time at The Game Awards, teases the Angels of Delusion faction

You may not come to The Game Awards for HoYoverse news, but the developer decided to surprise Zenless Zone Zero fans anyway and deliver some big news.

Zenless Zone Zero brought some hot new information and a first look at its next major faction as part of The Game Awards 2025 ceremony. As part of the showcase, we got a glimpse of Ye Shunguang and Zhao - two upcoming Agents.

The segment also teased the new Angels of Delusion faction, though details on that are slim.

The gameplay reveal for Ye Shunguang and Zhao was very much the highlight of what was ultimately a smaller segment. Ye Shunguang is Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent. She’s a Void Hunter who hails from Yunkui Summit.

Shunguang is a master swordswoman, and she can shift between two different forms. Her combat looks smooth and stylish, with a lot of aerial attacks and fast sword play. Zhao should be familiar to anyone who plays ZZZ. The rabbit Thiren has a bit of a slippery playstyle, quickly weaving across the battlefield to deliver attacks with her greataxe.

Before the trailer ends, we get the Angels of Delusion teaser, which didn’t offer much, but it’s certainly something for us to look forward to in the new year. In case you missed it, Zenless Zone Zero’s latest update - Version 2.4 - is live, having arrived over two weeks ago.

As ever, make sure to check out our updated Zenless Zone Zero codes if you plan to jump in over the next few weeks. Currently, ZZZ V2.4 is expected to run on a slightly truncated five-week schedule, with Version 2.5 now anticipated on December 30.

#4254. The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Updated (Version 1.1.1), Here Are The Patch Notes

Update [Wed 4th Nov 2026, 12:45pm]: The official patch notes have now gone live for Version 1.1.1 of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2.

It adds support for the Switch mobile app Zelda Notes and also fixes several issues to improve the overall game experience. Here's the rundown courtesy of Nintendo's Japanese support page:

After updating the software, please follow the instructions displayed at the start of the game to set up "ZELDA NOTES."

As Nintendo has previously explained, Zelda Notes allows you to see a record of your accomplishments, test your knowledge of the game, create and share your own ocarina melodies, and more. You don't need a Switch Online membership to use it, either.

You can find out the file size of this update and other information in the original story below:

Original Story: Some parts of the world are now just hours away from the launch of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2, and ahead of this, Nintendo has rolled out a new game update.

The anticipated release has been bumped from Version 1.0.0 to Version 1.1.1. Next time you check your game, you should be prompted to update. We had a look and can confirm our copy is also running on Version 1.1.1.

Based on the "manage software" section in the Switch 2 option menu, the remake is now 24.8GB in size, and this latest update is around 343MB to install. There are no patch notes just yet, but when we get an update about what's included, we'll let you know.

"Day one" and pre-release updates like this are pretty standard for Nintendo games nowadays, with the company often rolling them out to activate certain online features such as multiplayer. Star Fox also got a day one update when it returned earlier this year. Apart from overhauled graphics and gameplay updates, this latest remake includes support for amiibo and the Switch app Zelda Notes.

Again, if we hear any updates about this latest patch, we'll let you know. Have you been prompted to update your copy of Ocarina of Time yet? Have you got it digitally downloaded and ready to go, or are you picking up a physical copy? Let us know in the comments.

News The First Review For Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Is In

Liam is a news writer and reviewer on Nintendo Life. He's been writing about games for more than 15 years and is a lifelong fan of many iconic video game characters.

#4253. No more teasing, Arknights: Endfield finally has a January release date

Arknights: Endfield has been one of the most anticipated free-to-play 3D strategy games on the horizon, and it will be in our hands in the not-too-distant-future.

The Game Awards 2025 ceremony brought us yet more gacha game news, this time a big announcement for Arknights: Endfield. The free-to-play game set in the the universe of Arknights has been in various forms of closed tests for a while, but it finally has a release date.

The game is set to arrive simultaneously across PC, PS5, and mobile (iOS, Android) on January 22, and pre-registrations continue to be open.

Gryphline broke the news on The Game Awards stage alongside a chunky trailer featuring a new OneRepublic song. It actually ends up being a nice tone piece for the world of Arknights, showing a lot of cinematics alongside the music itself.

The developer-publisher also announced that so far, Arknights: Endfield has had over 30 million pre-registrations worldwide since pre-registrations went live. Some players have been able to play early, of course, with the most recent opportunity being Beta Test 2.

If you’ve been following the game’s development, you’ll know that it was pretty clear we’re closer than ever to the official launch. The most recent beta build showed off polished content, with new animations and cutscenes.

We’ve been playing it ourselves, and we think you’re going to agree with our Arknights: Endfield character tier list. You can expect more coverage from us as we get closer to launch, and when the game actually arrives.

Though it might seem like it came out of nowhere, the game is based on the Arknights universe, itself a massive mobile game with over 100 million downloads. Endfield brings a different flavour to that world, with a mix of strategy, exploration and real-time combat, not unlike the many games created by HoYoverse.

You can pre-register yourself on the official website.

#4252. Phantom Blade Zero: Here's How To Get The Perfect Ending, Which Is The Only Satisfying One

Phantom Blade Zero is a sprawling Wuxia adventure, the best action game of the year, and one of my favorite action games ever. It offers a lot to do, from main story quests to dozens of side quests, collectibles, hidden bosses, secret areas, and more. I highly recommend checking out Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks before jumping in. It mentions some tasks required to achieve the perfect ending, but here I'll break down exactly what you need to see it.

As a note, getting the perfect ending in Phantom Blade Zero isn't that unreasonable. It requires doing a lot of the game's side content, but it's not shrouded in mystery or puzzles; you just need to complete certain things before heading into the finale. I'm going to keep these requirements relatively spoiler-free, and honestly, without the wider story context, they'll be a lot of mumbo jumbo proper nouns that don't really mean anything. If you're set on getting the perfect ending, I'd bookmark this page, and as you play Phantom Blade Zero, more and more of these requirements will start to make sense. However, if you think even a name or proper noun is a spoiler, be careful reading these requirements.

The following requirements don't necessarily have a set order. You could technically ignore all of this and then go after everything right before the game's "last chance to get things done" warning near the finale. So don't sweat about picking up this or that at a certain time in your journey – do it when you want to. Just make sure you have the following requirements completed before heading past the "last chance" warning.

For more, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks, and then read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review.

#4251. How To Complete The Great Deku Tree Dungeon In The Ocarina Of Time Remake

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has finally been released, so grab your bottle of milk, load up your bomb pouch, and get ready to set off on one of gaming's most beloved adventures. Along this journey, you will encounter multiple large dungeons which make up a large portion of the story's challenge.

The first dungeon you will need to complete is the Great Deku Tree. If you're struggling to beat this or just want to know where all the Gold Skulltulas are located, here is how to fully complete this dungeon and find everything inside it.

Upon entering the Great Deku Tree, you will find yourself inside the main trunk of this being. In the middle of the floor is a large spider web. Around the perimeter of this room are various bushes and a new enemy: the Deku Baba. Unlike the version you encountered making your way to the Great Deku Tree, these will lash out at you. Use your shield to block and then strike them a couple of times to kill them.

Make a mental note of the spider web for now and head to the wall of vines. Climb up the vines, jump across the gap, and approach the large treasure chest. Inside you will find the Dungeon Map, which you can use to orientate yourself and see what areas you haven't visited. Continue up the path around the main chamber and go through the stone door.

Inside, you will encounter a Deku Scrub who hides underground whenever you get close. To defeat this enemy, hold up your shield and wait for it to spit a Deku Nut. This will bounce off the shield and ricochet back to the Scrub, knocking him from the ground. Rush over and slash at him a few times to trigger a brief dialogue exchange. He will explain that you can break your fall if you jump from a high place by holding forward.

I want them all, but that will require buying multiple copies of the game in various countries.

After beating the Deku Scrub, head through the door behind him to enter the next room. Inside, you will see another large treasure chest at the end of a large broken branch. Run across the branch to have it break apart under your feet, dropping Link to the floor below. Climb up the vines on either side to reach the chest, which contains the Fairy Slingshot.

Equip the slingshot by holding down R and then highlighting this weapon. Now, turn and face the Skullwalltula on the vines and lock onto it with Navi. Fire the slingshot at the enemy to kill it, climb the vines, and open the chest to receive a Rupee.

Jump back down to where you opened the chest and look at the way you initially entered the room. Above the door will be an eye, so hold down the right trigger to manually aim the slingshot and fire it at the eye. This will cause it to close and drop a stone ladder to the ground that can be used to return to the main chamber.

Once you're back in the main room, head to where you found the Dungeon Map, and use the slingshot to kill the three Skullwalltulas on the vines above the chest. If you don't, these Skullwalltulas will attack and knock you off the vines if you try to climb by them. With the enemies dead, go up the vines until you reach the next floor.

Head to the door, but don't just rush in, as a large Skulltula will fall from the ceiling. To kill this enemy, approach it until it starts to shake, and then quickly back up before it performs a spin attack. Wait until the Skulltula slows down and attack its glowing blue underbelly. Repeat this twice to kill this enemy, allowing you to access the room inside.

Go into the Compass Room and step on the stone switch to your right. This will cause three platforms in the center to temporarily rise up. Jump across them to the other side of the room where the chest is. To the left of the chest will be a Deku Baba, so kill it and then open the chest to obtain the Compass.

Now, move behind the chest, cut the grass, and climb through the crawl space to reach a hidden room. Go up the vines to find a small chest with a Rupee in it. Head back to the main Compass Room and go to the door you entered from to return to the main chamber.

The first Gold Skulltula in this dungeon can be found in the Compass Room. Before hitting the stone switch, jump down and head to the left side of the room. A Skulltula will drop from the ceiling, so kill it and then climb back up to where the switch is. Step on it to raise the stone platforms, go across them, and head to the opening on the left. Slash at the golden arachnid on the wall to earn your first Skultula Token.

Back in the main chamber, upon exiting the Compass Room, head left up the path. There will be two more Skulltulas you'll need to deal with until you reach the top. You'll find a part where a branch sticks out a bit over the main floor. Walk onto the branch and look down at the spider web. To reach the lower level, you will need to jump from where you are standing to the spider web below.

Doing so will cause the web to break, dropping you into the lower level. I recommend making sure you have gotten all the items and Gold Skulltula before doing this; otherwise, you will need to climb back up via a long vine wall, which is fairly tedious. When you reach the lower floor, climb out of the water, and head right towards the stone switch and unlit torch.

After landing in the water from falling through the spider web, turn immediately around and face the large vine wall leading back up to the first floor. On the vines will be a Gold Skulltula you can kill via the Fairy Slingshot. Hit it once, climb the vines, and grab your second token.

To the left of the stone switch will be another Gold Skulltula on some metal bars. Shoot it with your slingshot and then jump from the stone platform to reach the floating token.

With those two Gold Skulltulas acquired, step onto the stone switch next to the until torch to ignite it and burn away the spider web. Open the small chest to get some Deku Sticks and then equip one. Pull out a Deku Stick by hitting the Right Trigger and approach the torch with the stick to ignite it. Quickly, run across the stone platforms to the spider web covering the door and touch the burning stick to the web.

This will burn it away, allowing you to access the next room. Head inside and use your shield to dislodge the Deku Scrub. Run over to it and whack away at this enemy until it surrenders. The Deku Scrub will explain that you cannot defeat his siblings unless you deflect their projectiles in a specific order, which is 2-3-1. Use the Fairy Slingshot to shoot the eye over the barred door to unlock it and head into the next room.

In the next room there will be a moving platform going across the water that slides under a rotating spike log. To get past this trap, go into the water and dive down in the left corner to press an underwater stone switch. This will cause the water level to temporarily lower, so quickly climb back up to where you entered. Jump onto the platform and ride it, as you will now be low enough that you will pass right under the spiked log.

Go through the door to enter the next room and kill the Skultula that drops from the ceiling. After it's dead, move to the left of the large stone block and grab onto it with A. Push the block until it cannot be moved anymore and then climb up it to reach the door to the next room. Kill all the Deku Babas around the torch and then equip a Deku Stick. Use the stick to light the three unlit torches in each corner of the room to unlock the door.

When you go into the next room, you will be attacked by the Skulltula right as you enter. Once it's dead, a Gohma Larva will drop from the ground and hatch. Hold up your shield and wait for this enemy to launch itself at you. Block with the shield to stun it before swinging your sword. Once it's dead, look up at the ceiling, equip your slingshot, and shoot the two remaining Gohma Larva eggs to kill them before they drop to the ground and attack.

Gold Skulltula 4 Location — Gohma Larva Room (B1)

The fourth Gold Skulltula is located in the same room where you encountered the three Gohma Larvas. Take out the Deku Stick and burn away the spider web on the left via the torch. This will let you access the side room. Inside, kill the big Skulltula that drops from the ceiling, before using your slingshot to slay the Gold Skulltula on the vines. Climb up the vines to get the next Skulltula Token.

With the Gohma Larva dead, use your Deku Stick to burn away the spider web blocking the path to the right to proceed through the crawlspace. This will spit you back out into the lower main chamber, so approach the stone block and push it towards the water. This will cause it to drop and create a shortcut to where the ignited torch is located.

Equip your Deku Stick and head over to the torch. Light the stick and make your way back up the stone block to where the spider web on the ground is. Swing the lit Deku Stick while on the spider web by hitting ZR to burn it away. You will then fall into the water below and reach the lowest level of this dungeon.

Approach the three Deku Scrubs, but do not just block and attack each one. You need to ricochet their seeds back in a specific order, which was told to you earlier in the dungeon. The correct order you need to stun the Deku Scrubs is 2-3-1, with one being on the left and three being on the right. Once you block all the shots in the correct order, smack the remaining Deku Scrub with your sword.

This will cause him to give up, unlock the door, and leave a Rupee for your troubles. Equip the Fairy Slingshot and head inside the boss room.

Goham is the first boss of Ocarina of Time and, unsurprisingly, she's fairly easy to actually beat.

To start the fight, when you enter the room, look up at her glowing eye on the ceiling. Doing so will trigger a brief cutscene where she drops from the ceiling and begins the boss fight. When it starts, Gohma will protect her glowing eye with her mandibles while she follows you around the arena.

Upon getting close, she will raise both of her large limbs and then slam them down in front of her. Once the limbs go up, step back and wait for her to miss this attack. This will cause her to briefly become stunned, making her eye glow green, which is your signal to rush over and attack Gohma with your sword. After getting hit, she will retreat up the wall.

Equip your Fairy Slingshot as she climbs onto the ceiling and wait for her to stop moving. Aim the slingshot at her eye and shoot it to stun the boss and send her plummeting to the floor. Gohma will lie there for several seconds, so run over and start hacking away at her until she recovers and uses her mandibles to block her eye once more.

If you're not fast enough to take Gohma down from the ceiling, she will produce several Gohma Larvae that will join her in this fight. If this happens, prioritize the larva before refocusing on the boss.

You will then need to repeat this same process above at least two more times. Make sure to always wait until you hear the audio cue from Gohma when her limbs are raised, as this indicates she is committing to her frontal attack, and you can backflip away. If you run away too soon, she will not attempt to strike you.

Gohma will have no additional attacks or changes during this fight, so keep up the rhythm of baiting out her strikes and shooting her down from the ceiling until she is killed. You can now pick up the Heart Container to gain a full additional heart and complete this dungeon.

Dark Link is even more of an aura farmer than ever before in the Ocarina of Time remake.

#4250. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

#4249. The highly-anticipated follow-up to Baldur's Gate 3 is more Divinity, but it's not technically Original Sin 3

Larian has returned to tease a grand vision for its next major project, a new Divinity.

Larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

“This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

#4247. Former Xbox Manager Explains Why $500M Cost For Gears: E-Day Doesn't Tell The Whole Story

Update [Mon 2nd Nov 2026, 1pm]: Windows Central's Jez Corden has weighed in with a few extra details this morning as well, explaining that according to a "variety of trusted sources", The Coalition has been contributing to many other Xbox projects over the past 6-7 years.

All of these seemingly factor into the $500M budget that has been attributed, although it's unknown to what extent.

"...The Coalition worked for over a year and a half on a prototype project for Xbox that Windows Central understands was ultimately canceled. The Coalition also worked on Avowed, Hellblade 2, Clockwork Revolution, State of Decay 3, Grounded and Grounded 2, and has even contributed to the upcoming StarCraft reboot."

"The Coalition also spent a great deal of time working with Epic Games on the "Matrix Awakens" Unreal Engine demonstration, as well as the Alpha Point demo, both of which were intended to showcase the potential of UE5 on next-gen consoles and PCs."

Nevertheless, Corden warns that $500 million is a "lot of money to invest without a specific structure in place to explain why some of these costs were worthwhile to Microsoft auditors", and that there have even been "some internal disagreements over how exactly attribution should be distributed".

Original Story: Over the past couple of weeks, there's been a lot of chatter about a rumoured $500 million cost for The Coalition to make Gears of War: E-Day, alongside debates about how much of that money went on the game itself.

Speaking on the weekend, former Xbox exec Derek Reese shared his take on the situation, suggesting that The Coalition is heavily involved with supporting Microsoft's branch of the Unreal Engine, which is where a lot of the cost goes.

Here's what the ex-Senior Product Manager of Xbox Game Services had to say:

So much of that cost is The Coalition being on the hook for the Microsoft branch of Unreal and one of the flagship titles. I should know, I tried to get leadership to support a plan to have other studios adopt it and write off the support costs. Same problem with Turn10 and ForzaTech.

This aligns with what Jez Corden of Windows Central was saying a few weeks ago as well, who originally suggested that because The Coalition is "the technological glue for all of Xbox", some of that money is "spread across the entire portfolio" and even goes towards The Coalition's help on other Xbox games like Fable and Forza Horizon.

Corden confirmed yesterday that Reese's comments align with what he's heard:

In some follow-up posts, Reese mentioned that he thinks The Coalition "accomplished their end goals very well and delivered a great accomplishment in E-Day", while also suggesting that there's a "publicly visible pattern of allowing departments to shoulder the costs of leadership direction", pointing to Double Fine as a recent notable example.

So, hopefully we can put this one to bed now! It seems the $500 million budget IS a legit figure for Gears of War: E-Day, but it's hard to realistically attribute that entire figure to the game itself.

The big question is what Xbox thinks about all of this, including whether the game has been a success in terms of sales, Premium Upgrade conversions, Xbox Game Pass subscriptions and its pulling power as an Xbox console exclusive, and it could be some time until we know the answer to that.

Thanks to @fatpunkslim for alerting me to this!

I work in IT and have worked as an employee and contractor for my whole career. I also work with Microsoft contractors, and I will have to double check with them if what I’m going to say next also is true for them but I bet it is.

ANY well managed corporation has a time management system where employees and contractors register their time and what project they were working on. Even if they are salaried employees that don’t get paid by the hour. This is used not only to track personal time off and/or sick time but also precisely to manage independent project budgets.

It can sometimes be annoying as an employee that works full time in a single project (as those employees might see it as pointless), but it’s vital for management to know what projects (not teams) are eating up money.

If Xbox has been operating exclusively around team hierarchy to evaluate project expenses, then Xbox has been managed way worse than I expected.

Even if it was, it would had been prudent of self-piloted studios to at least internally implement such tracking precisely so they could protect their own operations should this ever come up, precisely as it’s implied in the article. If they are seriously having issues tracking the accreditation of tome contributed to other studios/teams projects, then the Coalition management also was doing a terrible job. I’m not talking about project leads, I’m talking about anyone in charge of time keeping. At this point, I would not be shocked if no one was in charge of timekeeping, though.

It was pretty obvious it wasn't JUST Gears E-Day, from the additional comments said last week, but it's good to have more sources say it.

That said $500+ million is still a lot to spend on a studio with only one game releasing, even if it was also supporting other games that will bring in revenue & some tech/demos that won't, at least not directly.

Either way I hope Microsoft and Xbox can attribute some of the revenue of those other games back to the Coalition, because it seems like E-day didn't sell very well despite it being brilliant, and they could do with the support.

Mean does it really change the overall point of the conversation?

@Fishmasterflex96 Not much imo. It's still the operational cost of the studio, regardless where it was spent. But it does soften it a little. Fingers crossed for The Coalition.

While it's good that the full picture has been revealed, it's very concerning how these rumours were handled by people still at Xbox. If you respond to rumours then if you're silent about other rumours, people come to the conclusion the rumours not addressed are the full truth. Especially when insiders like Jason Schreier get involved.

Xbox were very quick to address stuff like terrible GTA6 Xbox preorder numbers rumour and the MW4 Xbox review issue but when it comes to this E-Day budget rumour, they were just silent.

“Nevertheless, Corden warns that $500 million is a ‘lot of money to invest without a specific structure in place to explain why some of these costs were worthwhile to Microsoft auditors,’ and that there have even been ‘some internal disagreements over how exactly attribution should be distributed.”

It’s a very, very bad time for any team at Xbox to be costing lots of money and unable to point to direct attribution.

I have to imagine some of this budget (however big or small) was going to the PS5 port, with the plan to recoup more of the cost there. I really hope that Xbox leadership has taken that into account, since it was enough of a last-minute decision that the trailer went out with the PS5 logo.

Exactly. Still shows the inflated cost of AAA development mainly in North America. To be clear this isn’t just an Xbox issue. But will say one thing that affects mainly only affects Xbox is having their super expensive AAA games launch on game pass day one taking away a huge chunk of revenue from a full purchase which on top of the increasing development cost certainly doesn’t help.

I don't know why some people believe unfounded rumours so quickly and why the same people don't believe official sources when they revoke them, e.g., "Xbox is on sale", and the behaviour only applies to Xbox, in a suspicious way, to make it look like it's always failing.

The fact that The Coalition has been working on multiple games, not just theirs, just confirms that they are one of the best assets that Xbox has. This is not a new thing, they have been doing that for many years. Id has been doing the same to a lesser extent, e.g., they helped Bethesda with Starfield.

This is why you can't just say that an Xbox cost $500M. You could say so about a third party whose budget was leaked and that was focused on a single game, but not about an Xbox studio.

#4246. Street Fighter 6 'Winter Pocket Present' Fighting Pass Adds Super Gem Fighter Mini Mix

Capcom continues to roll out regular updates for Street Fighter 6, and it's now lifted the lid on its "Winter Pocket Present" Fighting Pass, arriving this week.

This new pass is themed around the 1997 arcade chibi-style title Super Gem Fighter Mini Mix (aka Pocket Fighter) and includes all sorts of rewards inspired by this classic game.

This includes more EX-Colors, new titles, more music, seasonal avatar gear, more challenger screen illustrations, new emotes & stickers, and the retro title, which you can access via the title's arcade section. Here's a look at everything included and you can see it all in motion in the video above.

This isn't the first time Super Gem Fighter has been revived. Apart from being playable in Street Fighter 6 via the game's Fighting Pass (made up of free and premium tiers), it can also be accessed in the Capcom Fighting Collection, which is available for Switch. It's also in the collection series Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium.
