#4245. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4244. Phantom Blade Zero: Longtime Sonic, Ezio Voice Actor Roger Craig Smith Is The New VO For Protagonist Soul

Longtime Sonic the Hedgehog voice actor Roger Craig Smith, who also voices iconic characters such as Ezio Auditore, Chris Redfield, and Batman, is the new voice of Phantom Blade Zero protagonist Soul, according to developer S-Game. Smith replaces former voice actor Jay Maksenuk, who can still be heard voicing Soul in various trailers and gameplay videos.

You can hear Smith's rendition of Soul in the official launch trailer for Phantom Blade Zero, however, below:

Game Informer has reached out to S-Game for a comment or statement on why the VO was changed and will update this story if it learns more.

I can pull back the curtains a bit on how last-minute this change seemingly was for Phantom Blade Zero. For most of my time playing Phantom Blade Zero for review (you can read it here), Soul was still voiced by Maksenuk. I wasn't the biggest fan of the English VO at the time, so I played most of the game using its excellent Chinese VO. However, about a week into the review period for Phantom Blade Zero, developer S-Game told me the VO for Soul had been updated (the team had previously said this update would happen ahead of time).

S-Game didn't say why or who at the time, but after listening to it post-update, it was clear to me it was Smith; his voice is iconic and hard to miss. I was basically at the end of the game at that point, so I didn't get to hear too much, but overall, I like Smith's inclusion as Soul's VO.

Nonetheless, if you're jumping into Phantom Blade Zero at launch, the Soul you play as will be voiced entirely by Smith. Let us know in the comments what you think of it after you've had some time with it!

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review, and then check out these Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks.

#4243. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#4242. Where To Find All 100 Gold Skulltulas In The Ocarina Of Time Remake

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has finally been released, which means it's once again time to search high and low for shiny spiders. Just like the N64 version, players will be tasked with locating all 100 Golden Skulltulas scattered throughout the lands of Hyrule if they want to complete everything in the game.

This is easier said than done since this is a remake and not just a remaster. Meaning, not all of the Gold Skulltula Tokens will be in the exact same spot they were in the original game. So if you want to ensure you grab them all during your playthrough or just want to check to see which Gold Skulltulas you are missing, here is a complete list of every single one, sorted by location.

Unlike other side quests in this game, you can actually start the Gold Skulltula side quest by simply finding them in the world. However, things come into focus once you reach Kakariko Village. When you arrive, look for a massive house on the southeast side of town near the graveyard entrance.

This is the Skulltula House, which contains a cursed family who are looking to regain their humanity. To do so, Link will need to break the curse by killing and collecting all 100 Gold Skulltula tokens. These are Skullwalltulas that have an ornate, glowing gold torso that can be found in nearly every single location in the game.

Gold Skulltulas are also prevalent in both the past and present settings of the game, with some being exclusive to that time period. When hunting for them, listen for the audio cue that sounds like constant scratching, as that will let you know when you're close. Some Gold Skulltulas you encounter won't be collectible right as you discover them, so you'll need to return once you have a specific item.

Additionally, once you unlock the Echo Gem, this will put an icon on the left side of your screen that blinks when you are near a Gold Skulltula spawn point. Even if it's daytime, the gem will pulse and make an audio cue if you get close to where it will spawn at night. I highly recommend always having it equipped if you're hunting for all 100 Gold Skulltulas.

There are a total of six rewards that unlock as you progress through this quest. Each one is tied to hitting a specific milestone, and you can collect your rewards by talking to the people at the Skulltula House.

My recommendation is to bookmark this guide and then use the Jumplinks on the left side of the page. This will let you instantly jump to the specific area you are in, letting you see which Gold Skulltulas you will encounter while exploring that location.

At the Bottom of the Well, once you have the Lenses of Truth, make your way to the northwest corner. There will be a door that leads to a room with several Fire Keese and a Beamos. Kill all of them and use the Lenses to avoid the pitfalls to the basement. Go through the southern door to enter the Like Like Room. Defeat the lone Like Like and you'll find the Gold Skulltula on the eastern wall.

While in the Bottom of the Well, there will be two locked rooms in the central chamber. In order to open the first one, go along the outer path and grab the Small Key in a chest you can see by using the Lenses of Truth along the eastern side where the big Green Bubble is patrolling. Take the Small Key back into the inner area and unlock the door in the back left corner. There will be a Gold Skulltula on the wall you can collect.

The second locked room in the center of The Bottom of the Well can be opened by heading to the far west side of this mini dungeon. Dive under the arch in the water and then climb up to the door. Go inside, kill the Gibano, and then use a Deku Stick to burn away the coffin between the torches. This will reveal a Small Key. Bring this back to the middle, open the other locked room, and use the Leneses of Truth to walk along the hidden path to the Gold Skulltula.

Death Mountain Crater Entranceway — Young or Adult Link

To get this Gold Skulltula, climb to the very top of Death Mountain and go inside the massive entrance. The moment you enter, hang a left and run towards the two wooden crates. Break the farther of the two crates and kill the Gold Skulltula inside. You will be quickly burning to death from the moment you enter the crater, so do not waste any time! Get the token and leave.

For this Golden Skulltula, progress through the story until you learn the Bolero of Fire from Shiek. Once this happens, warp back to the Temple of Time and swap to young Link. Now, get a Magic Bean and a bug in a bottle. Play the Bolero of Fire and teleport there as a kid. You won't have much time, so quickly look for the bug hole right by the warp point. Use the bug to coax out a Gold Skulltula, kill it, then plant a Magic Bean in the soil so you can return to this spot and ride the flower to also get a Piece of Heart!

You can obtain this Gold Skulltula once you're given the ability to pick up and throw Bomb Flowers. After you blow open the cave entrance to this dungeon, go to the cave opening you just created. On the right side, before you go into Dodongo's Cavern will be a bug hole you can drop a bug into via a bottle. Just like all the other bug holes, a Gold Skulltula will pop out for you to kill.

Between Dodongo's Cavern And Kakariko Village — Young or Adult Link

The next Gold Skulltula on Death Mountain Trail can be unlocked once you have completed Dodongo's Cavern and obtained the Bombs. On the path from Kakariko Village to this dungeon there will be a bombable wall along the right side. Place an explosive by the cracked wall to destroy it and access the Gold Skulltula on the other side.

After beating the Fire Temple, go to the top of Death Mountain where the Biggoron is. Just below where you can talk to him, there will be a large grey rock you can break with the Megaton Hammer. Shatter it to find a Gold Skulltula.

Once you have the Megaton Hammer, go outside of Goron City and look for a large grey rock along the cliffside. Hit it with the hammer to reveal the Gold Skulltula behind it.

Bomb Flower Staircase Room (2F) — Young Link

Your first Gold Skulltula in this dungeon is located at the top of the room where you formed a staircase via detonating all the Bomb Flowers. At the door, turn around and face the large wall that has netting on it. There will be both a normal Wall Skulltula and a Gold Skulltula. Use your Fairy Slingshot to kill them both and climb up to get your token.

The second Gold Skulltula can be found in the side room to the southeast of where you were first introduced to the Armos Statues. In the hall with the Baby Dodongos, you will find a cracked wall you can blow open with a Bomb. This will reveal a small chamber with a Gold Skulltula and three normal Keese.

Another Gold Skulltula can be found to the right of the switch you used on the second floor to turn the platform into an elevator. Next to the suspension bridge over the Dodongo Skull, use a bomb to blast open the breakable wall and head inside. There you will find two Dodongos around a large rock. Kill the enemies and go to the back of the rock to find the next Gold Skulltula.

The final Gold Skulltula in Dodongo's Cavern can be found in the block room. Before you push the block embedded in the wall, move the block on the ground so it's in front of the cracked wall. Drop a bomb on top of the block so it blows open a hole to a side room. In this new area, you will find a hostile Armos Statue and three Baby Dodongos. Kill all of them, and you can find the Gold Skulltula along the back wall.

One of the easiest Gold Skulltulas to miss, this one can be found as adult Link. When you enter Dodongo's Cavern, head southeast down the hall where all the buried Baby Dodongos are. Kill these enemies, then look along the northern wall about halfway down the hallway. There will be a Scarecrow spawn point just above you. Play the Scarecrow Song to summon him, then use the Hookshot to pull yourself up so you can reach this elusive Gold Skulltula.

The first Gold Skulltula is located to the north of the Spirit Temple entrance. Along the wall, near the giant flock of enemy birds, you will see the Gold Skulltula on the wall.

Once you learn the Requiem of Spirit, play the song to warp back to the Temple of Time and switch to young Link. Then play the Requiem and go up to the Spirit Temple entrance. To the left will be a Bug Hole, which causes a Gold Skulltula to pop out when you drop an insect from an Empty Bottle into it.

Magic Bean Flower (Night Only) — Adult Link

The last Gold Skulltula in this area can be obtained once you've planted a Magic Bean into the Bug Hole. Return to this spot as adult Link and ride the Magic Bean Flower to the second massive rock. On top of the rock you will find the Gold Skulltula.

To get this Gold Skulltula, go to the large lava cavern on the first floor and head to the back left corner. There you will find a square platform that rises up when stood on. This will put you in front of a block that can be teleported via playing the Song of Time. Go into the next room which has several enemies waiting for you. Once you've defeated both the Flying Tiles and Like Like, you can find the Gold Skulltula on the wall at the back of the room.

You can find the second Gold Skulltula in the boulder maze. From the entrance, head down the slope and go right to the north side of the room. Along the corner on the northeast side of the room, you will find a bombable wall. Drop an explosive next to it to blow it open and reveal a Gold Skulltula behind it.

Once you push the block down from the fire wall chase room, jump onto the platform with the Flame Slug and kill it. Look up the wall you just came through, and you'll see a Scarecrow spawn point. Play the Scarecrow Song to summon him and use your Hookshot to pull yourself up. Then grapple to the small elevator directly across from the Scarecrow. In the next room at the very top there will be a Gold Skulltula on the wall.

Directly after getting the previous Gold Skulltula, go through the door and look to the right. You will see the spider on the wall, which you can kill and snag the token with the Hookshot.

In the second Flying Tile Room, which is accessible by using the Megaton Hammer on the statue in the Entrance Room, you will find a large grey rock along the back wall. Use the Megaton Hammer to break the rock, revealing the Gold Skulltula right behind it.

Our first Gold Skulla can be found at the Forest Temple entrance. At the very top of the tree covered in vines will be a Gold Skulltula. Kill it with the Hookshot and snag the token.

Conveniently, your next Gold Skullatula can be found near the top of the stairs on the north side of the Grand Hall. At the top of the stairs, turn to your right, and you'll see the spider clinging to the wall. Like the previous one, use your Hookshot to kill and take the token it leaves behind.

On the second floor of the garden where you emptied the well, carefully walk out onto the ledge to the left of the door. Follow it around the corner until you see the Gold Skulltula in front of you. Use the Hookshot to kill and grab the token.

The fourth Gold Skulltula in the Forest Temple is located outside of the Boss Room. Rotate the room via the pillar a total of four times until the green-colored chamber with the pots is accessible. Go inside and look up at the wall to find the Gold Skulltula.

Your final Gold Skulltula in the Forest Temple can be found in the West Garden. After you've pushed the large block down to make a shortcut, look above you at the small balcony to see a Scarecrow spawn point. Play the Scarecrow Song to summon him and then use the Hookshot to pull yourself onto the balcony. There you'll find the Gold Skulltula.

Once you've unlocked the Hookshot, go to the exterior of Ganondorf's Castle and head to the left. On the ruins of what was Hyrule Castle gate will be the Gold Skulltula. Use the Hookshot to kill and grab the token it leaves behind.

Fortress Exterior (Night Only) — Adult Link

After you've completed the Gerudo Fortress and obtained the Gerudo Pass, use your ocarina and play the Sun Song to make it nighttime. Then head west side of the fortress, and in a small gap by a door where you can spawn the Scarecrow, you will find the Gold Skulltula clinging to a wall.

Horse Archery Range (Night Only) — Adult Link

This Gold Skulltula is located at night in the horse archery range to the south of the main fortress. When you arrive, go to the farthest target, and on the back will be the spider. Get close to the fence and use the Longshot to kill it and take the token it leaves behind.

Gerudo Valley Entrance (Night Only) — Young Link

You can obtain this Gold Skulltula once you've obtained the Boomerang from the third dungeon. Make your way to Gerudo Valley at night and go into the water below the makeshift plank bridge. Under the bridge at the far end will be the Gold Skulltula you can kill.

Another Gold Skulltula you can nab is right when you enter Gerudo Valley as Young Link. Make your way to the suspension bridge, grab the nearby Cucco, and fly down to the water below. Land near the large waterfall and climb onto the path. Follow the stream on the path to find a lone Gerudo Warrior with a cow. Near them will be a Bug Hole you can drop a bug into to get a Gold Skulltula.

Carpenter's Camp 1 (Night Only) — Adult Link

As an adult, cross the bridge to the Captenter's Camp in Gerudo Valley. Go across from the tent towards the stone arch where all the large grey rocks you can smash with Megaton Hammer are. Above those rocks, along the column supporting the arch, will be a Gold Skulltula you can kill with a Hookshot.

Carpenter's Camp 2 (Night Only) — Adult Link

Staying at the Carpenter's Camp, you can find this one on the wall directly behind the tent at night.

To get this Gold Skulltula you will need to have unlocked the bombs from Dodongo's Cavern. Upon entering the city, take a left and use your bombs to blow up the talls rocks. Continue following the path until you see a bunch of rocks all clustered together. The grey ones cannot be destroyed, so you'll need to make a path via the normal looking ones. Think of this like a maze, but you're making a path with explosions. You want to destroy the first rock on the right, go down the path, and blow up the next one on the left. Then blow up the rock on your right. This will let you access the back of the room where there are two small chests and a Gold Skulltula hiding in a wooden crate.

Your second Gold Skulltula in Goron City can be acquired as adult Link once you've gotten the Hookshot. Go to the city and head to the second floor. Make your way to the north side and look up at the central rock that is suspended over the middle of the city. There, you will find the Gold Skulltula clinging to the rock.

The first Gold Skulltula in the Great Deku Tree can be found in the Compass Room on the third floor. Before hitting the stone switch, jump down and head to the left side of the room. A Skulltula will drop from the ceiling, so kill it and then climb back up to where the switch is. Step on it to raise the stone platforms, go across them, and head to the opening on the left. Slash at the golden arachnid on the wall to earn your first Skultula Token.

After landing in the water from falling through the spider web in the main chamber, turn immediately around and face the large vine wall leading back up to the first floor. On the vines will be a Gold Skulltula you can kill via the Fairy Slingshot. Hit it once, climb the vines, and grab your second token.

In the same room you fell into via the spider web, look to the left of the stone switch to find another Gold Skulltula on some metal bars. Shoot it with your slingshot and then jump from the stone platform to reach the floating token.

The fourth Gold Skulltula is located in the same room where you encountered the three Gohma Larvas. Take out the Deku Stick and burn away the spider web on the left via the torch. This will let you access the side room. Inside, kill the big Skulltula that drops from the ceiling before using your slingshot to slay the Gold Skulltula on the vines. Climb up the vines to get the next Skulltula Token.

Upon entering through the gate of Hyrule, take an immediate right and go through the door. At the back of the room will be two wooden crates. Roll into the one closest to the guard to break it, revealing a Gold Skulltula you can kill inside.

Your next Gold Skulltula can be found outside of Hyrule Castle. Make your way up the main road past the guards at the gate and go into the first courtyard where the three soldiers are. At the end of the courtyard, where the vine wall is that you normally climb; there will be a tree on the right. Roll into the tree to dislodge the Gold Skulltula, allowing you to kill it and get the token.

For this Gold Skulltula, you will need to first learn the Song of Storms from the man in the windmill as an adult. Once you have, return to the past and go towards the castle like when you woke Talon up with the Cucco. In a corner, there will be a large plant with three leaves flat on the ground behind a tree. Play the Song of Storms next to it to make the hole open. Jump down, blow open the bombable walls, and grab the Gold Skulltula with the Boomerang.

Available once you're playing as adult Link, make your way directly west of the Kokiri Forest entrance. There will be a lone, skinny tree right by where the river ends. Go to the tree and roll into it to knock a Gold Skulltula loose.

In the future, make your way to the southeast corner of the map near Lake Hylia. There will be a pseudo-wetland with a bunch of Tektites hanging around shallow pools of water. In the water, there will be a hole that you can blow up with a bomb. Look for a grey cracked circle on the ground, as this is where you need to place the explosive. Jump down the hole, and you'll find the Gold Skulltula in a wooden crate.

The second Gold Skulltula in Hyrule Field is located just west of the Lake Hylia entrance. Go into the forest with all the Deku Scrubs and hug the rock wall. You will find another bombable hole that you can jump down into. Kill the big Skulltula and then look up to find the next Gold Skulltula. Use the Hookshot to kill and take the token it leaves behind.

In the Spinning Blade Room, look to the left from the door you enter. Up high on the ice wall will be a Gold Skulltula. Stand off to the side, away from the spinning blade, and use your Hookshot to snag this token.

In the Compas Room, approach the chest where you got this item and look to the left. In a small carved out section of the ice column will be the Gold Skulltula. Kill it with the Hookshot and snag the token.

In the west block puzzle room, make your way through the stalagmites and approach where you actually move the ice cube around the room. Turn around and face the way you came to find a Gold Skulltula on the wall above your head. Use the Hookshot to kill and snag this token.

The first Gold Skulltula in Kakariko Village can be found near the town entrance from Hyrule Fields. When you enter the village, go to where the Foreman's son is sitting and roll into the tree. This will knock out a Gold Skulltula, which you can kill and get a token from.

On The Watch Tower (Night Only) — Young Link

The next Gold Skulltula is located on the tall watchtower near the center of town. Look for where the tall ladder is; you can climb to the top, and you'll find the spider clinging to the tower. Shoot it with your Fairy Slingshot to kill the Gold Skulltula, and then climb up the ladder to collect the token.

Construction Site (Night Only) — Young Link

Now go from the watchtower to the south, where the construction site is. On the wall facing the pen where the Cucco Lady is, you'll find the Gold Skulltula.

Behind The House (Night Only) — Young Link

Head up to where the soldier is by the gate to Death Mountain to the north and look for a house to his left. Behind the house, you will find a Gold Skulltula on the wall.

Skulltula House (Night Only) — Young Link

The next Skulltula is located right outside of the large Skulltula House where all the cursed people are. When you approach the door to go inside, you'll find the Gold Skulltula directly to the left.

Go to the graveyard to the east and head up to the small incline. Go to the left, and by a tree you will see a bug hole. Release a bug in a bottle to make the Gold Skulltula appear, allowing you to kill it.

Behind Dampe's House (Night Only) — Young Link

Another Gold Skulltula you can get once you acquire the Boomerang. Return to Kakariko Graveyard once you have this item and go to Dampe's House. Behind it, on the right by the fence, will be the spider.

Your next Gold Skulltula in Kakariko Village can be acquired once you have the Hookshot. Go to Impa's House in the south and look for a large collection of vines above your head on the cliff to the left. Use the Hookshot to pull yourself to the vines, climb onto the roof of her house, and use the Hookshot again to kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall.

The first Gold Skulltula in Kokiri Forest can be found behind the store where you initially bought the Deku Shield. This one will require that you have a bottle with a bug inside. Go behind the store and look for the bug hole mound. Equip the bottle and dump the bug onto the dirt to make it crawl inside. This will force the Gold Skulltula out, allowing you to kill it.

Know-It-All's House (Night Only) — Young Link

Your second Gold Skulltula is found at night behind the Know-It-All Brothers' house. This is in the southwest corner of the village, and you can find the Gold Skulltula on the trunk of the tree.

House of the Twins (Night Only) — Adult Link

In the future, you can get this Gold Skulltula once you have unlocked the Hookshot. Go to where the store is and look for the House of the Twins directly across from it. Behind the house, above the ground, will be a Gold Skulltula.

Our first Gold Skulltula in Lake Hylia can be found in the southernmost part of the region. When you arrive, swim all the way across the lake, past the trees and islands to the rocky cliffs. Look for a lone Blue Tektite guarding a small hole that you can crawl through. Squeezng through this space will spit you out into a small room with a Gold Skulltula on the wall.

The next Gold Skulltula is found right outside of the Lakeside Laboratory on the northwest side of the region. When you get to the door, look to the right, and you will see a bug hole you can drop an insect near. This will, like all the other bug holes, force a Gold Skulltula to pop out that you can kill.

Lakeside Laboratory Wall (Night Only) — Young Link

For this Gold Skulltula, you can only acquire it once you have the Boomerang or Hookshot. Return to Lake Hylia at night and walk onto the suspension bridge next to Lakeside Laboratory. Look at the back wall once you're on the bridge to see the Gold Skulltula.

Once you have the Iron Boots and Zora Tunic, return to the Lakeside Laboratory and go inside. Jump into the dive tank and sink to the very bottom. Now, roll into the wooden crate to free the Gold Skulltula, then use the Hookshot to kill it so you can grab the token.

Once you have the Longshot, go to the central island in Lake Hylia where the large tree is. Use the Longshot to reach the top of the tree where you will find the Gold Skulltula.

The first Gold Skulltula in Lon Lon Ranch can be found behind the large house on the left when you enter through the gates. Look for a skinny tree and roll into it. This will knock down a Gold Skulltula that you can kill.

On Malon's House (Night Only) — Young Link

Your next Gold Skulltula is located on the front of Malon's house at night. Approach the building and look up over the door to find the Gold Skulltula on the window. Kill it with your Fairy Slingshot and use the Boomerang to pick it up.

Your third Gold Skulltula at Lon Lon Ranch can only be obtained once you get the Boomerang or Hookshot. Go to the southwest corner of the ranch and head inside the ruined stone tower. Once inside, look up, and you'll see the Gold Skulltula clinging to some vines.

Your first Gold Skulltula in Lord Jabu-Jabu can be found in the Dungeon Map room. After you raise the water, swim over to the vines directly across from the large chest and climb up to the elevated area. Kill the Gold Skulltula clinging to the wall to claim your prize.

This Gold Skulltula can be acquired once you have the Boomerang and clear out all the parasitic tentacles. Drop down the hole in the main chamber to find this bug clinging to the northern wall.

In the same room as the previous Gold Skulltula, this one is on the wall in the hallway that leads to where you fight Big Octo. Just look up and to the left when you enter the hall to find this Skulltula.

You can find the last Gold Skulltula in this dungeon right outside of the boss room where the large column is. After defeating the Biri, you can find the spider clinging to the vines on the column, so use your Boomerang or Fairy Slingshot to kill this enemy. Now just climb up and claim your token.

The first bug hole in the Lost Woods can be accessed by going Left and then another Left when you enter this area via the Kokiri Forest. After you make the second left, you will find the bug hole immediately to your left. Drop a bug from a bottle next to it to force a Gold Skulltula to spawn.

The next Gold Skulltula is located deeper in the Lost Woods. From the Kokiri Forest entrance follow this exact path through each of the "doors": Right, Left, Right, Left, Left. This will spit you out into a room where there are two Deku Scrub Vendors whom you will need to stun by deflecting their shots with your shield. Once they're dealt with, you'll find another bug hole in the back right corner of the room. Drop a bug from a bottle there to obtain another Gold Skulltula.

In the same bug hole mentioned above, plant a Magic Bean seed into the ground. Then return to this meadow as an adult and step onto the flower. It will raise you up to a small section containing a Gold Skulltula that you can kill.

The only Gold Skulltula in the Mirage Desert can be found about halfway through the desert when you reach a small abandoned temple. Take refuge from the storm inside the temple and go down the ladder to the lower chamber. From there, you will find the Gold Skulltula on the wall by some unlit torches

When you're headed to the Forest Temple as Adult Link, make your way through the maze filled with Moblins. Before going down the straight path towards the Moblin wielding the mace, turn around and go up the ladder to get on top of the maze. You will find the Gold Skulltula to your left, so use the Hookshot to kill it and grab its token.

In the Invisible Scythe Room, after you've killed all the enemies, go through the unlocked door and on the back wall you will see a Gold Skulltula.

Before crossing to open the small chest in the spike crusher room, you will find the Gold Skulltula high up in the northeast corner of this room. Use the top of the crusher traps to reach the small area where it is, and then use the Longshot to snag the Gold Skulltula.

At the end of the hall full of fans, cross the gap with the Hover Boots when the fan stops blowing and then use the Iron Boots to stop from being blown away. Turn and face the way you came to find a Gold Skulltula on the bottomless pit wall. Use the Longshot to kill and secure the token.

On the dock, before you board the Ghost Ferry, look above where you pulled the stone block to see a Scarecrow spawn point. Take out your ocarina and play the Scarecrow Song to summon him, and then use the Longshot to pull yourself up to it. Directly to the left of the Scarecrow will be a Gold Skulltula.

Located north of the invisible maze after the Ghost Ferry docks, in this room you will see three massive skull vases that are spinning around in a circle. Go up the stairs and equip your bombs. Throw the explosive into each of the vases to shatter them. One of them will contain a Gold Skulltula and a ton of Rupees. Once the Gold Skulltula is free of the vase, run down the stairs and kill it.

Your first Gold Skulltula in the Spirit Temple can be acquired right after you drop part of the fenced wall to make a bridge. Kill the Gold Skulltula with a Boomerang and use the same item to safely collect this token.

At the base of the massive statue on the right, you will find the Gold Skulltula nestled in the northeast corner.

In the hallway between the Iron Knuckle Room and the Silver Diamond Room you will find a Gold Skulltula above the door. Use the Boomerang to destroy the Gold Skulltula and claim your token.

In the Rolling Boulder room, go to the back left corner (northwest) to find the Gold Skulltula in a small nook. Remember, if you played the Song of Time to move the block, you'll need to play that tune again so you can slay this spider!

After getting the Small Key from the chest on the Colossus Statue's hand, look up to the northwest corner to see a Scarecrow spawn point. Play the Scarecrow Song on your ocarina to summon him, then grapple up to the ledge it's on. You'll find a Gold Skulltula right next to him.

The first Gold Skulltula can be obtained once you raise the water level up, so the surface is on the second floor. Instead of going out into the Main Chamber, equip the Iron Boots and sink to the bottom of the tower. With the block raised, the opening in the floor will be accessible. Drop down, kill the three spikes, and use the Hookshot on the gem switch. This will open a gate in the ceiling. Float up into the next room to find the Gold Skulltula along the wall.

Behind The Bombable Wall (2F) — Adult Link

The second Gold Skulltula in this dungeon can be accessed when the water level is set so the surface is the second floor. Go to the east side, use the Iron Boots to go to the ground floor, and then enter the room where you initially met Ruto. Unequip them to float to the surface, and you'll see a cracked, bombable wall on the east side. Blow it open, kill the Shell Blades inside, and you'll find the Gold Skulltula on the western wall.

Your next Gold Skulltula in the Water Temple can be acquired in the underground cave system right after you get the Longshot. Follow the river underwater, and at the first bend to the right, the Gold Skulltula will be above the water on the wall. You will be underwater during this, so look for the gold shimmer of the spider and use your Longshot to kill it and acquire this token.

Now that you have the Longshot, you can snag the Gold Skulltula on the ceiling of the central tower in the Main Chamber. Use the Longshot to travel up the grapple points, then look up to find the Gold Skulltula in a corner. Use your new tool to kill and snag the token!

The final Gold Skulltula in the Water Temple can be found in the hallway where the boulder rolls that connects to the Boss Key Room. Look up and along the wall; behind a small waterfall will be the Gold Skulltula. Use your Longshot to kill it and secure your prize.

In the future, when you are adult Link, make your way to Zora's Domain and go to where you participated in the diving mini-game. To the left, you will find the Gold Skulltula clinging to the wall. Use the Hookshot to kill and snag the token.

Outside The Great Fairy's Fountain — Young Link

You can find the first Gold Skulltula at the Zora Fountain near the southeast corner of the region where the Great Fairy's Fountain is located. Look for a lone tree that has a golden glow near the top. Roll into it to dislodge the Gold Skulltula so you can kill it and claim the token.

The second Gold Skulltula in Zora River can be found along the southern wall. Look for the submerged arch and wall making a makeshift ramp. Directly across from them will be a Gold Skulltula high up on the wall. Because of this, you'll need either the Boomerang or Hookshot to obtain this token.

This Gold Skulltula can only be acquired once you get the Silver Gauntlets from the Spirit Temple. Return to this area and go to the southeast corner near the Great Fairy Fountain. Use the Silver Gauntlets to toss aside the rocks, then activate your Lenses of Truth. There will be several invisible Skulltulas throughout the cave. Fight your way to the top, then play the Sun Song to make it night. Over the vines you climbed to reach the top will be the Gold Skulltula.

The first Gold Skulltula in Zora's River can be found right next to the Magic Bean Salesman. Directly to the right will be a bug hole that you can drop an insect into. In the original game, this was the only hole that actually didn't contain a Gold Skulltula, but one moved in for the remake!

End of the River (Night Only) — Young Link

To find this Gold Skulltula, make your way to the very end of the river upstream and jump down to the lowest level. You will see a stone column that is holding up part of the makeshift bridge. Behind the pillar will be the next Gold Skulltula.

Zora Domain Entrance (Night Only) — Adult Link

In the future, go to Zora's River once you have the Hookshot and make your way to the very end where the entrance to the Zora Domain is. Along the northwest wall, high above, you will see the Gold Skulltula. Normally, you're supposed to get this with the Longshot, but if you stand on the stone railing, you can actually just reach the Gold Skulltula to kill it and take the token.

Middle of the River (Night Only) — Adult Link

As adult Link, once you've unlocked the Hookshot, return to Lake Hylia. If you plant a Magic Bean in the spot right by the man who sold them in the past, there will be a Magic Bean Flower here in the future. Step onto the flower and ride it to the middle section you originally could reach via a Cucco. Step off the flower onto the raised section and jump across the small gap. You'll find the Gold Skulltula on the wall, so use your Hookshot to snag it.

#4241. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

And, in case you missed it, below is an image of the PC system requirements and specs needed to play Phantom Blade Zero on Steam and the Epic Games Store:

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review, then check out our list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks we wish we knew before starting the game. Then check out our breakdown of the requirements to see the best ending in the game.

#4240. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

#4239. Zenless Zone Zero's big end-of-year update brings multiplayer combat, free Zhao, and the first dual-form Agent

Zenless Zone Zero' is saying goodbye to 2025 with a bang, as update 2.5 gets fully revealed.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered the good news on Version 2.5, To Be Fuel for the Night. This chapter is a big deal for a few reasons, not least of which because it brings an end to Season 2.

To start with, Version 2.5 arrives on December 30, making it the game’s last major update of the year, which also means players are in for some freebies to celebrate the new year.

Of course, the biggest addition in Version 2.5 is Ye Shunguang, the game’s new Agent, who’s a Void Hunter, and also Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent. Zhao also becomes a playable Agent as part of this update - two things HoYoverse teased last week at The Game Awards.

Ye Shunguang’s unique attribute is Honed Edge, through which she can enter an Enlightened Mind state. Ye Shunguang’s signature Ether Veil can deliver Honed Edge damage as she applies a vulnerability effect to enemies. She arrives alongside her sidekick, Bangboo Sprout, who keeps with her swordplay theme by calling down flying swords.

Zhao is the other playable Agent as mentioned, an S-Rank Ice Defence legend. Zhao is a fast and nimble attacker who uses her giant greataxe to suppress enemies. Zhao can trigger Ether Veil: Wellspring by using Frostbite she accumulates, which buffs the entire squad.

Narratively, this particular chapter will reveal the fate of Waifei Peninsula. The quest is gonna take the squad deeper into the Lumite Mine ruins, and the new Perception Technique is how you’ll uncover the answers hidden within.

There’s a gameplay component to that, too. Ye Shunguang's Bladeflash Mirage ability will come in handy during the story’s big investigation, which comes with unique rewards, including a new W-Engine.

Version 2.5 is also the one set to give players the first taste of multiplayer combat thought he limited-time Joint Investigation: The Divine Maze event. As part of that, you can have three-Agent squads face off against each other in unique combat challenges.

There’s even more to get excited about in this one. Proxy Outpost lets you create your own Outposts, and join those created by other. This is more of a social feature than anything, though.

HoYoverse is also making a series of updates to Soldier 11, Grace, Soldier 0 – Anby, Ellen, and Burnice, all of whom will see their mechanics updated and their effectiveness boosted. Similar updates are on the way for other Agents, which will arrive in future updates. Shiyu Defense and Deadly Assault has seen some adjustments to the gameplay loop, too.

Finally, HoYoverse is making it easier for players to jump into 2.5’s new story chapter using Advance Screening. Ye Shunguang and Zhao will be available for the entire update’s duration, and reruns in the second half will guarantee another S-Rank.

You’ll be able to pick from Alice, Soldier 0 – Anby, or Astra. Zhao will herself be available as a login bonus alongside 1,000 Polychromes, a new outfit for Jane, and more. If you’re looking to jump in on December 30, don’t do so without having a look at our Zenless Zone Zero codes page to get some freebies.

#4236. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Is Reportedly Still "More Than Two Years Away"

After initially announcing The Elder Scrolls 6 all the way back in 2018, Bethesda has now officially confirmed its subtitle: Sentinel. Ooh.

However, if you're under the impression that this means the game is somewhat imminent, a new post from Bloomberg's Jason Schreier suggests that it is still "more than two years away" (thanks, Push Square).

I think a lot of people forget that The Elder Scrolls VI was only announced in 2018 (along with Starfield) to soften the blow of Fallout 76 — "Don't worry, even though we're making a multiplayer game we've got single-player stuff coming too!" Sorry to say this game is still more than 2 years away!

This, of course, would likely mean that its eventual release will land at least a decade following the game's announcement at E3 2018, which is frankly just ridiculous. And we thought the eight-year wait for Metroid Prime 4: Beyond was overkill.

It's just yet another indication that studios need to exercise some restraint when it comes to early announcements. As Schreier stated in his post, Bethesda seemingly wanted to balance out its Fallout 76 announcement with the promise of another single player-focused Elder Scrolls game, but we're not convinced anybody could have predicted what a long wait it would turn out to be.

Nintendo is pretty good at keeping its announcements under lock and key until the right moment these days, and we suspect that Prime 4 proved a big lesson for the company in this regard. Hell, Zelda: Ocarina of Time was only properly announced in June this year, and it's launching tomorrow at the time of writing. Can't argue with that!

#4235. FC 26 adds upgraded Pina alongside 3 new Heroes in full Winter Wildcards promo

Winter Wildcards Team 1 is scarier than Ultimate Scream, featuring buffed Pina, Dembele, Valverde and Rodman cards alongside brand-new Heroes.

EA Sports has revealed 3 new Heroes coming to FC 26 Ultimate Team as part of Team 1 of the Winter Wildcards promo: Ivan Zamorano, Claudio Pizarro and Jill Scott.

The Bayern and Werder Bremen legend Claudio Pizarro is famously the Bundesliga’s oldest ever player, after turning out well past 40 years of age - up front no less. But he’s making an appearance in FC 26 because he won the Hero Vote Poll a few months ago, with the Peruvian edging out notable nutter Steffan Effenberg and the prolific Brazilian striker, Elber.

The love for South American Heroes continues with Ivan Zamorano presented in his Real Madrid guise rather than part of the unbelievably stacked Inter squad which featured legends and Icons ranging from current Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone to Javier Zanetti and Ronaldo Nazario.

And probably most interestingly, Queen of the Jungle and centurion Lioness, Jill Scott, is also coming to shore up the midfield with a card which fits the “Gullit Gang” pre-requisite of all face stats over 80 - including a dominant 91 physical befitting her role as one of the most recognisable enforcers in women’s football.

Whether her in-game body type will actually let her put that strength out on the pitch (she will surely also have Bruiser) remains to be seen, but she could easily have the gangly aura of Patrick Vieira if the rest of her PlayStyles are right.

New Ultimate Team Heroes have been added mid-season before, including the likes of Enzo Francescoli in FC 24, but 3 at once looks to indicate that EA is leaning on Heroes to add fan-favourite players to the game with a lower threshold than Icons.

Plus they can be given away for free without upsetting the power curve as much as Icons, as shown by the free Classic XI Heroes handed out recently (I got Mario Gomez, F).

The rest of the Winter Wildcards team features a host of equally famous, and now infamous, players with some featuring 99 stats and alternative positions.

Highlights include striker and CAM versions of Balon D’or holder Ousmane Dembele, but also everyone’s love-to-hate Low Driven Shot master, Claudia Pina.

There are also incredibly strong-looking Gabriel and Fede Valverde cards, as well as downgraded, and therefore hopefully cheaper, versions of Icons like Johan Cruyff.

For more on how to get the most out of these players, check out our round-up of the best formations in FC26. Or for some Career Mode legends, try out the best FC 26 Wonderkids.

#4234. The Duskbloods Delayed To 2027 So FromSoftware Can Adjust 'Game Rules And Balancing'

While the 2025 reveal of the Switch 2 came with many surprises, none were as unexpected as The Duskbloods. It's a Switch 2 exclusive, multiplayer-only title from FromSoftware, the developer behind games like Dark Souls and Elden Ring; in other words, not your typical Nintendo game. While The Duskbloods was originally scheduled to launch sometime this year, today the developer announced it's pushing the game's launch to 2027.

According to a post on The Duskbloods' X account, the main reason for the delay was balance-related. Here's the full statement:

While development of "The Duskbloods" is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027. We apologize to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support. During the network test, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including combat, strategic depth, and player expression. To further enhance these aspects, we have decided to move the launch, allowing time for final adjustments to game rules and balancing.

We attended a hands-on preview session earlier this year and came away very positive, and sentiment was similar following the game's closed network test (that is, when the servers were working properly). It's not surprising that the devs have changes in mind following so much public feedback, though it is a little surprising that it will take until sometime next year for those adjustments to be complete.

To tide you over until the game's launch, check out our in-depth preview impressions or watch the video above to hear our live commentary over gameplay footage. You can also hear us discuss the game on our podcast, The Game Informer Show.

#4233. Where To Find All The Empty Bottles In The Ocarina Of Time Remake

There are a lot of collectibles to find in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. From Pieces of Heart to Gold Skulltulas to all the different ammo capacity upgrades, you can easily spend several extra hours hunting everything down. While some of these can be overlooked, one collectible you'll want to acquire is the Empty Bottles.

There are five in total, four of which can be missed if you're not willing to explore or engage in side activities. So you want to ensure you have every bottle available; here is where to find all of them.

Your first Empty Bottle can be acquired as soon as you visit Hyrule Castle Town after the Great Deku Tree. When you arrive, make your way into the town square and look for the store with the large potion display over the door. Go inside the Potion Shop to find the vendor freaking out behind the counter about an escaped bug.

Talk to him to learn that he needs help locating the insect and will offer you the Empty Bottle to do so. Turn around from the counter and use the bottle by pressing ZR to swipe it across the ground next to the bug crawling around. This will put it into the bottle, and the vendor will reward you with a free Red Potion for your troubles. You can also now use the Hyrule Castle Town potion shop whenever you want.

And nearly 850 times the size of the original.

The second Empty Bottle can be unlocked once you venture into Kakariko Village for the first time. Go to the south and speak to the red-haired woman by the empty pen to learn that all seven of her Cuccos have escaped. Thankfully, locating all of them and throwing them back into the pen will earn you an Empty Bottle.

Using the photo above, you can find all the Cuccos here:

Once you have returned all the Cuccos, go talk to the red-haired woman again and she will reward you with your next Empty Bottle!

Your third Empty Bottle is located at Lon Lon Ranch in the past. Located in the middle of Hyrule Field, make your way to the ranch during the daytime and go into the first door on the left when you enter. Inside you will find Talon sleeping among a ton of Cuccos. Speak to Talon to wake him up, which will prompt the ranch owner to ask if you want to play a mini-game.

The game requires you to find three "Super Cuccos" that he will randomly throw out into the group of birds in the room. You will then have thirty seconds to pick up all three correct birds, which will earn you another bottle that will be filled with milk. While the Super Cuccos are basically indistinguishable from the normal ones, you can get an idea of where they were when Talon throws them at the start.

Pay attention to what direction the birds are going and then start picking up whatever Cuccos are where they could have landed. There aren't a lot of Cuccos, so there's a good chance you will easily grab the right ones. Upon finding all three Super Cuccos you'll earn the third bottle.

This one is unmissable, as you will get this Empty Bottle by progressing through the main story. Once you arrive in Zora Domain, you will be tasked by King Zora to find his daughter. To do this, you'll need to first earn the Silver Scale via the diving mini-game. This can be found by going up to where King Zora is and then looking to the left.

There you will see a lone Zora standing near the top of a waterfall. Speak with him and agree to play his mini-game, which requires you to dive into the water below to obtain five scales before the timer hits zero. Completing this mini-game once will earn you the Silver Scale, allowing you to dive deeper than normal.

Once you have the Silver Scale, go to the bottom of the Zora Domain and look for a large stone opening underwater. Dive and swim through the opening to be spat out in Lake Hylia. When you emerge, there will be several Zora looking for any signs of Princess Ruto. Underwater in the ruins will be a single Bottle with a message from her in it.

Grab the bottle and return to the surface to add it to your collection. You can now freely use this bottle as you see fit!

The final Empty Bottle is going to require the most amount of work. First, you will need to unlock Epona and complete the Forest Temple so you have the Fairy Bow. Once you have both of these, go to Hyrule as adult Link and enter through the main gate. To the right, where the guard room with all the pots used to be, the Poe Collector will set up shop.

They will request that you bring them Big Poes to earn a special reward. There are ten in total (all locations shown above), but for the Empty Bottle you just need to collect five of them. This is done by going to the locations throughout Hyrule Field and looking for either a large tree branch or a stone wall with a purple lantern on it.

Jumping over this while on Epona will summon a Big Poe, which you'll need to chase down and kill by hitting it with two arrows. Doing so will cause the soul to drop, so quickly get off Epona and put it into a jar. Sell five of these Big Poe souls to the Poe Collector and you will earn the fifth and last Empty Bottle in the game!

#4232. Assassin’s Creed Franchise Update Reveals Codename Hexe News Coming Next Year, New Game Plus for Valhalla, And Confirms No New Remakes

Ubisoft has released a fall update on the Assassin’s Creed franchise, providing news big and small on its flagship series. The news includes updates for existing games and smaller but significant insights on the various upcoming Assassin’s Creed games previously announced.

In terms of current games, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is getting a long-requested New Game Plus thanks to a new update coming on November 5. This means you can start a fresh game while bringing over your progression items/level from your previous playthrough. This update will also introduce the following features:

This news comes a few days after New Game Plus arrived in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

Codname Invictis, a PvP multiplayer game, remains in development as Ubisoft shares it has incorporated feedback from players who, according to Ubisoft, “saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed.” To this end, Ubisoft has spent months reworking Invictis to reflect this vague feedback and say the game is “now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions.”

As for the next single-player Assassin’s Creed, Codename Hexe, Ubisoft says it will share the next major update on this game in 2027. First announced in 2022, Codename Hexe is set during the 17th-century reign of the Holy Roman Empire, and the era's witch hunts will play a significant role.

With the release of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this year, Ubisoft has given fans what they'll likely see as a disappointing update on potential future remakes: “One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development. Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories.”

However, Ubisoft adds that this door isn’t closed for good. “Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back,” says Ubisoft.

Ubisoft’s next update concerns the live-action Assassin's Creed series in production for Netflix. They say the show is “nearing completion” in Rome and that award-winning composer Hannah Peel (Insomnia, Rogue Agent, Game of Thrones: The Last Watch) is composing the score.

Lastly, Ubisoft teases big celebrations are planned for 2027, which marks the 20th anniversary of the Assassin's Creed franchise. It's keeping details to itself for now, but states it's "preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and community moments. "

For more on Assassin's Creed, check out our review of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

#4231. Heartopia finally gets a release date... on everything but Steam

Heartopia may very well be the first big game you play in 2026.

Heartopia developer XD Games has delivered the news anyone who tried out the life sim game had been waiting for. The Animal Crossing-like cozy multiplayer game will finally arrive on January 7 across Android, iOS, and PC - with one caveat.

The Steam version won’t actually launch on that date, and will instead go live at some other point in the future. You will be able to play it on PC through TapTap, which is the same emulator you may be familiar with from beta.

Pre-registration is open on the official website for all platforms. If you throw in your email address, you’ll receive a bundle of in-game items at launch. You’ll get 4,000 Gold, 20 Wishing Stars, 400 Moonlight Crystal, and 60 Exhibition Passes.

Interestingly, XD Games isn’t saying what you can expect from the launch build - in terms of content - just yet. Those details will be revealed closer to the January launch, so perhaps expect them in the first few days of the year.

If you created a character in either (or both) of the recent closed beta tests, you’ll also receive the Blueberry Crossbody Bag in-game cosmetic. If you made it to level 18 in either test, you’ll also get the Star Mascot Head cosmetic. Both items will be available to claim at launch.

We’ve spent a lot of time playing the game’s recent tests, and we’ve put together some early guides on how to get Roaming Oak Timber, how to unlock and upgrade hobbies and more. We also have a few cooking recipes to share with you.

From the original North American launch on November 15, 2001

Welcome to the month of Xbox's 25th anniversary! Xbox will be celebrating that milestone officially on November 15th, but before we get there, we thought we'd use the chance to highlight the very first games that ever launched on Xbox.

To do that, we're going back to the initial list of North American Xbox launch titles, of which there were 20 in all. Some of them are obvious standouts, such as Halo: Combat Evolved, Fuzion Frenzy, Dead or Alive 3 and Project Gotham Racing, while others are more obscure - Arctic Thunder, Dark Summit, Mad Dash Racing, etc.

Here's the full list of all 20 launch titles:

Now, of course, some of these games are still playable to this day on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, while others have always remained locked to the original Xbox. The likes of Project Gotham Racing, Shrek and Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2x are highly-requested additions to the Xbox backwards compatibility library, but it seems unlikely they'll ever make the cut at this point - almost certainly due to licensing reasons.

However, you may not know that games like Cel Damage and Oddworld: Munch's Oddysee are still playable to this day on modern consoles, and they're still well worth checking out despite their age.

#4229. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

#4228. Sir Patrick Stewart, Star Trek, X-Men, And Myriad Video Games Actor, Passes Away

According to a report from The Hollywood Reporter, actor Sir Patrick Stewart has passed away at the age of 86. Stewart spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, shared that he died after “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.”

Stewart was best known for his roles as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation (and its various spinoffs) and Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, but he did plenty of video game performing, too. Stewart played Emperor Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, one of the first characters you meet in the game, and Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. He also played Jean-Luc Picard in about 10 different Star Trek games and Charles Xavier in five different X-Men games.

Stewart will always be a crucial voice and face in the legacy of sci-fi entertainment. Jean-Luc Picard will undoubtedly be an enduring and important character in the Star Trek franchise, and that's thanks to Stewart's portrayal of the starship captain. His portrayal of Charles Xavier also helped to legitimize the comic book movie, and he will appear again as the character in this year's upcoming Avengers: Doomsday.

Our thoughts are with his friends and family, and the millions of fans (of which I include myself) who are mourning his loss. Let's all drink some Earl Grey tea in his honor today.
