#4209. How To Complete Dodongo's Cavern In The Ocarina Of Time Remake

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has officially launched, so grab your Hylian Shield, load up your Fairy Slingshot, and get ready to save Hyrule once again. Throughout this journey, you will need to complete several dungeons that are filled with traps, puzzles, combat encounters, and a unique boss at the end.

One of the first dungeons you'll be tasked with completing is Dodongo's Cavern, which is located right outside of Goron City. This is a far more elaborate dungeon than the previous Great Deku Tree and will be your first real challenge if you're new to this title. If you're struggling at all or just want to ensure you find all the collectibles inside, here is how to find and do everything in Dodongo's Cavern.

After going through the massive hole you created on Death Mountain's Trail, you will enter a smaller room with a breakable wall at the back. Since we're currently limited to Bomb Flowers, grab one of the two Bomb Flowers and throw it at the rocky entrance to blow open the door to the actual dungeon. Step inside to trigger a brief cutscene introducing Dodongo's Cavern.

Dark Link is even more of an aura farmer than ever before in the Ocarina of Time remake.

Now that we're in the dungeon, you will want to head to the left side of the Main Chamber. Be careful as you traverse across the platforms, as they not only sink into the lava below, but you'll also need to contend with the new Beamos enemies. These foes fire a laser in a straight line that chases after you. You can either outright avoid them since they cannot move or destroy them with a Bomb Flower.

Make your way left and destroy the Beamos with the nearby Bomb Flower. Once it's dead, take the Bomb Flower and destroy the destructible wall near the back left corner of the room to reveal a large chest that contains the Dungeon Map inside. Additionally, you can use the Bomb Flower to destroy the other breakable wall on the left side to find a small chest that has a Blue Rupee in it.

After getting the Dungeon Map, head to the right side of the Main Chamber, taking extra care to not get attacked by the Beamos in the center. Just like before, grab the Bomb Flower and use it to destroy the Beamos on the right, before using it to blow open both of the breakable walls on either side of the elevated section.

In the back right corner will be a Gossip Stone, and the path forward will be in the bottom right corner. Progress down the tunnel and kill any of the Baby Dodongos that come scurrying out of the dirt. These explode a few seconds after taking damage, so always try to keep your distance from them after you swipe at these foes with your sword.

There's a Gold Skulltula you can get once you are playing as Adult Link. Return to the hallway with all the Baby Dodongos and look along the northern wall about halfway down the tunnel. Above you will be a Scarecrow point you can reach with the Hookshot via the Scarecrow Song! We can't do anything about it now, but it's good to come back to!

Once they're dead, approach the door with the stone switch in front of it. Push either of the two Armos Statues on top of the switch to permanently unlock this door. Progress through the hallway with the two Keese and go out the door on the other end.

When you enter, the door will lock behind you, and you'll need to kill two Lizalfos.

These enemies are quite nimble and will only attack you one at a time. Play defensively and use your shield to block their attacks before swiping at them with your sword a couple of times. After one takes a few hits, it will run away, and the other will take its place. Repeat this process of blocking their initial strike and counterattacking when they stop. There's no point in chasing after them, so just stay on the platform you entered on until both are defeated.

With the Lizalfos dead, a chest will spawn with a Red Rupee inside. You can also refill your hearts by hitting the pots on either side of the arena. Go into the next hall and use the Bomb Flower to blow open the cracked wall on the right. This will reveal a Business Scrub who is selling Deku Nuts and Deku Sticks if you need them. If not, progress into the blue-colored chamber directly ahead of you.

Make sure to have the Hylian Shield for this dungeon! If you have the Deku Shield equipped and take fire damage, it will burn up, and you'll need to get a new one!

In this room, there will be three Dodongos, which are slow-moving but relatively dangerous enemies. Their weak points are their tails, as the rest of their bodies are heavily armored. Approach one and wait for it to breathe fire before running behind it and slashing at its backside. Hit it twice and then back away to avoid its tail swipe move. Repeat this process two more times to kill the Dodongo.

Now, you do not need to actually fight these Dodongos if you want, but it does make the small puzzle in this room easier if you're not being harassed by angry lizards. Once they're dead, take out a Deku Stick and light the three unlit torches in this room. There will be one by the closest and farthest pillar, with the third being against the right wall.

This will unlock the door, letting you go inside. You're now back in the main chamber, so step on the stone switch to unlock the door directly across from you. Jump back down into the main chamber, head across the moving platforms, and go into the newly unlocked door.

Proceed into the next chamber and use a Bomb Flower to blow open the breakable wall directly to your left. Inside will be three Armos Statues, with one sitting directly in front of the ladder. Upon interacting with the Armos Statue by the ladder, it will come to life and attack Link. Equip your Deku Nuts and use them to stun the enemy, freezing it in place. Now quickly grab a Bomb Flower and throw it at this foe to kill it. Don't stand too close, as it will explode when it dies.

Approach the ladder and climb it to reach the chest that contains the Compass.

With the Compass and Dungeon Map acquired, the next task is to acquire the Bomb Bag so you can carry and use Bombs wherever you want. Upon leaving the room where you got the Compass, head over to the large stone pillar that is surrounded by Bomb Flowers. You'll notice a gap in the middle, so grab the lone Bomb Flower that's off to the right side and place it in this opening.

When the Bomb Flower detonates, it will cause a chain reaction where all the other Bomb Flowers around the pillar will explode in sequence. If done correctly, all the Bomb Flowers should explode, causing the pillar to shift, revealing that it's actually a staircase. Climb up the stairs and continue up the dirt incline until you reach the next door.

Gold Skulltula 1 — Bomb Flower Staircase Room (2F)

Your first Gold Skulltula in this dungeon is located at the top of the room where you formed a staircase via detonating all the Bomb Flowers. At the door, turn around and face the large wall that has netting on it. There will be both a normal Wall Skulltula and a Gold Skulltula. Use your Fairy Slingshot to kill them both and climb up to get your token.

In the next room there will be two Fire Keese and four Armos Statues surrounding a central platform. Use your Fairy Slingshot to kill the fiery bats and then approach the platform in the center. Three of the four Armos Statues around the platform are hostile, with the only inanimate one being in front of a ladder. All the hostile ones will have broken ladders behind them, so check for the one that has an intact ladder, pull the statue away, and climb up to activate the switch, opening the door.

Go across the bridge above the Main Chamber and kill the Fire Keese flying around you. In the next room there will be two spike traps moving horizontally across the ground between the series of pillars. Time your movements carefully and go to the back right corner. Grab the movable block and push it towards the lower pillar near the ladder.

Use the block to reach the pillar, which will let you both access a small chest that has some Deku Seeds and a Bomb Flower. Grab the Bomb Flower and toss it at the cracked wall by the ladder to clear a path. Now move the block in front of the ladder and use it to climb up to the opening you just created.

Continue into the next room where there is a large flame blocking your path. Take out your Fairy Slingshot and shoot the eye above the door, behind the fire to temporarily stop the blaze. Quickly cross the platforms and go into the next room. There will be several Baby Dodongos buried in this room, so carefully deal with them as you cross the lava to the door in the back left corner.

The next room will have two more Lizalfos that you'll need to deal with. Just like before, use the Hylian Shield to do your best turtle impersonation and wait for the Lizalfo to attack. Once it hits the shield, the enemy will be briefly stunned allowing you to get a couple slashes in before going back on the defensive.

Use this method to defeat both Lizalfos to unlock the doors and spawn a small chest. Before proceeding, go to the far end of the room and make your way through the narrow gap in the rocks. There you will find the newly spawned chest which contains a brand-new item called a Business Scrub Seed. When used, this seed will spawn a Business Scrub anywhere in the game, allowing you to buy items you might need. When you're done, head through the unlocked door on the left side of the Lizalfo arena.

In the next room, you will need to once again shoot the eye switch to make the flames on the platform cease. Hit the eye switch directly across from you first, then jump onto the platform that no longer is lit. Quickly look to your left to see a second eye switch and use your slingshot to also shoot this. Doing so will cause the second platform's fire to vanish, letting you safely cross.

You will then reach a room with a large chest which finally contains the Bomb Bag. This allows you to carry up to 20 bombs and use them anywhere you want! Blow a hole in the wall behind the chest with your newly acquired explosive and continue into the Main Chamber.

Now that we're back in the main chamber, we need to make our way to the boss' room. Step onto the switch to activate the platform on the ground floor to turn into an elevator between the different levels. If you want another Gold Skulltula, take the platform down to ground level, otherwise, go to the suspension bridge over the Dodongo Skull.

The second Gold Skulltula can be found in the side room to the southeast by where you were first introduced to the Armos Statues. In the hall that had the Baby Dodongos you will find a cracked wall that you can blow open with a Bomb. This will reveal a small chamber with a Gold Skulltula and three normal Keese.

Gold Skulltula 3 — Suspension Bridge (2F)

Another Gold Skulltula can be found to the right of the switch you used on the second floor to turn the platform into an elevator. Next to the suspension bridge over the Dodongo Skull, use a bomb to blast open the breakable wall and head inside. There you will find two Dodongos around a large rock. Kill the enemies and go to the back of the rock to find the next Gold Skulltula.

Once you're done getting all the Gold Skulltulas, head onto the suspension bridge over the Dodongo Skull. There will be two conveniently bomb-sized holes in the bridge that are above each eye socket. Drop a bomb into both eye sockets of the skull to light up the eyes and cause the jaw to open, revealing a new door you can go through. There will also be an additional bombable wall that has a small chest behind it that contains a Blue Rupee.

Make your way back down to the first floor of the Main Chamber and go through this newly opened door.

Upon entering through the door in the skull, make your way down the hill and then go up the incline on the other side. Ignore the switch on the floor for now; we will come back to it. Follow the path until you reach a room with several stone blocks. Grab the stone block directly to your left and line it up with the one on the raised section.

Doing so will let you climb onto the block you moved and push the one on the raised section to the area below. Now, head down to where you pushed the block and drag it to the back left corner of this room. Move your block so it's aligned with the one in the wall. Climb onto the block you've been pushing around and shove the one in the wall forward so you can reach the next section.

The final Gold Skulltula in Dodongo's Cavern can be found in the block room. Before you push the block embedded in the wall, move the block on the ground so it's in front of the cracked wall. Drop a bomb on top of the block so it blows open a hole to a side room. In this new area, you will find a hostile Armos Statue and three Baby Dodongos. Kill all of them, and you can find the Gold Skulltula along the back wall.

Follow the path back down to the room with the switch and push the stone block in front of you onto the lower level. Then drag the block into the conveniently block-sized hole with the switch at the bottom. Dropping the block onto the switch will unlock the boss room door.

The big bad of this dungeon is the massive dinosaur, King Dodongo. This hulking behemoth is far easier than he actually looks. Your main weapon during this fight will be bombs, so make sure you have a few before dropping into the hole you make in the boss's room. When you hit the ground, a brief cutscene will play that introduces the boss.

Right after you regain control of Link, equip the bombs and wait for King Dodongo to begin sucking air and fire into his mouth. Throw a bomb at his mouth while the boss is sucking in air to make him eat the explosive. This will detonate inside King Dodongo, stunning him and causing him to collapse onto the ground.

Quickly run over to King Dodongo and begin slashing at his tongue to damage him. Keep it up until he stands back up and closes his mouth. Now, run to any corner of the room and stand on the edge near the lava. King Dodongo is going to start rolling around the arena, but you can entirely avoid this attack by just hanging out where the lava and ground meet.

Once he slams into a wall, a few Baby Dodongos will spawn and rush towards you. Deal with enemies and wait until King Dodongo begins sucking in air once again. If you're fast enough, you can throw a bomb into his mouth and kill the Baby Dodongos, but if not, you'll need to avoid the massive fireball he launches. This projectile will ricochet around each side of the room.

Nothing else in this fight will change, so keep throwing bombs into his mouth, attacking his tongue while he's stunned, and using the edge of the arena to avoid his attacks. The only difference is he will summon more Baby Dodongos the second time he recovers from being attacked. Otherwise, this is an extremely straightforward fight.

After killing him, he will roll into the lava and turn to stone. A Full Heart Container will spawn, so make sure to grab it before stepping into the light and teleporting outside of the dungeon's main entrance.

And nearly 850 times the size of the original.

#4208. Full FC 26 Team of the Year promo brings free Hero upgrades and another unstoppable Claudia Pina

The FC 26 Team of the Year brings new end-game special cards for meta favourites and Icons, as well as upgrades for free Heroes.

EA Sports has revealed the much-anticipated Ultimate Team of the Year cards for the 2025/26 season, including a slew of meta favourites from the likes of the evergreen Virgil van Dijk, super-fast Kylian Mbappe and unplayable queen of FC 26 Claudia Pina.

Elsewhere Lionesses Alessia Russo, Lucy Bronze and Leah Williamson feature alongside now-obligatory Barcelona duo Alexia Putellas and Aitana Bonmati. On the men’s side, Arsenal’s title tilt sees Declan Rice and William Saliba make the first 11, while Champions League holders PSG have the most players from a single team, with Ousmane Dembele, Vitinha and Nuno Mendes adding both rapid speed and technical prowess to proceedings.

However, the Team of the Year selection hasn’t been without controversy. The FC 26 TOTY promo is voted for by players, you probably cast your vote by selecting time-limited gold cards yourself, but that method has led some to question whether the Team of the Year is more of a popularity contest than a true measure of performance. This is with specific reference to Virgil, whose in-and-out form during Liverpool’s poor start this season has caused some to question his eight-straight inclusion.

In yet another blow to those of us who got Mario Gomez and Gianluca Vialli from the Classic XI Hero pack, during the TOTY event these Classic XI Heroes will be further upgraded to TOTY Honorable Mentions Heroes.

More TOTY items will also be dropping over the next couple of weeks, including a men’s and women’s 12th player, Honorable Mentions, 2 teams of TOTY Icons and both a men’s and women’s “Captain of the Year”.

#4207. Two Big Remasters Are Now Lined Up For Xbox On December 3rd

Including a first-ever Xbox appearance for the original Thief!

It's usually the case that December is a quiet time for new video game releases, but we've still got a few notable ones lined up for the first couple of weeks on Xbox, including two very interesting remasters on December 3rd.

We already knew about the first of these - Rayman Legends Retold is coming to Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S on that date. It seems a little bit redundant to "reimagine" an Xbox One game like Rayman Legends on the face of it, but the previews have been pretty great for the most part, and there's no doubt that Legends is a great game in general.

The next one has just been announced for December 3rd today though, and it's Thief: The Dark Project Remastered. The original Thief has never appeared on Xbox before, having first released on PC back in 1998, but it was considered one of the best games of that year across any platform, and has a whopping 92 average rating on Metacritic.

Its remaster is being handled by the experts at Nightdive Studios, known for an absolute ton of great remasters in recent years, so as long as you don't mind the dated nature of it, this could end up being a must-buy on the 3rd.

Exciting stuff! We'll leave you with more details on both games down below.

On this page: Two Big Remasters Are Now Lined Up For Xbox On December 3rd

Embark on a bold reimagining of the acclaimed platformer, filled with new content and narrative twists. When a shadowy villain spreads corruption across the Glade of Dreams, journey through its charming worlds solo or in up to 4‑player couch co‑op in a fast‑paced, side‑scrolling adventure where every stumble and surprise adds to the delightful chaos.

In Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, Nightdive Studios brings back the pioneering 3D stealth game from Looking Glass Studios. Described by its developers as a “first-person sneaker,” the 1998 title challenged norms with its non-confrontational gameplay at a time when most first-person games prioritized combat. Thief was the first stealth game to use light and sound as game mechanics to help you hide from and sneak up on characters, rather than simply attacking them. Remastered with Nightdive’s KEX Engine, the release includes Thief: The Dark Project and the additional missions, content and updates from the 1999 Thief Gold re-release.

#4206. Switch Cartridges Under Threat As Key ROM Manufacturer Exits Business

Move may accelerate transition to digital

Macronix, one of Nintendo's key ROM manufacturers for physical game cartridges, is ceasing the production of ROM altogether.

This comes via analyst David Gibson who relayed the news from Macronix's latest financial release. According to the data, ROM products accounted for just 5% of the firm's overall revenue for Q3 2026, representing a stark decrease of 39% year-on-year.

It will now shift its focus over to NOR and eMMC memory chips instead, and will no longer report ROM sales separately in its future financial releases.

Gibson is keen to stress that Nintendo will have other partners to utilise when it comes to the production of cartridges, but this move may nevertheless accelerate the transition to digital game sales alongside Game-Key Cards.

Digital sales have already made up more than 60% of Nintendo's total sales during Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, but this tends to fluctuate based on major game releases.

It'll be interesting to see whether Nintendo itself addresses this development in its own financial release, which it due to drop this week on 5th November. Even if it doesn't acknowledge it in its own material, it seems likely that the question will arise in the company's usual Q&A session. We'll keep an eye out and relay its reaction and plans going forward.

For now, it's likely business as usual for Nintendo, but we'll be interested to see just how this affects the production of physical cartridges in the future and whether it will indeed accelerate the transition to digital.

Update: There are conflicting reports as to whether or not Macronix supplies ROM for Switch 2 specifically. For now, we've removed the mention of 'Switch 1 & 2' from the headline and will investigate further. We'll update this piece as soon as we're able to clarify.

#4204. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

#4203. Shigeru Miyamoto Proclaims November 1 is Pikmin Day, Pikmin 4 Demo Coming To Switch 2 Soon

This morning, Nintendo shared some updates related to the Pikmin franchise and has officially claimed November 1 as Pikmin Day, starting today and moving forward presumably forever.

Aside from the announcement of Pikmin Day as a general idea, Pikmin creator Shigeru Miyamoto appeared on camera to remind everyone that Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is coming November 12. A free demo for the game, which will include one standard level and two Dandori Academy levels, will be available on November 2.

The Switch 2 version of the game (you can read Game Informer’s Pikmin 4 review here) will have improved visuals and take advantage of the Switch 2’s mic to let you say things like “Rush” and “Go to work” to Oatchi. The Dandori Academy side of the game is essentially time trials you can practice, and then on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, you will have one chance to post your best time. You can read more about the Switch 2 version of the game here.

Miyamoto also shared that the mobile game, Pikmin Bloom, is also getting a fairly substantial update soon with secret caves. In Bloom, players will be able to find maps that reveal caves that you can send your Pikmin into to battle and find treasure. You can also find maps for Bloom by playing Pikmin 4. Caves will be coming to Pikmin Bloom later this year.

The Pikmin Day presentation also reminded viewers that every Pikmin game is available on Switch and Switch 2, though no announcements or hints were made implying that Pikmin 1 and 2 would be coming to the Nintendo Switch Online subscription service, which includes GameCube games on Switch 2. Those games can be purchased individually on the eShop.

Finally, Miyamoto brought actress Fuka Koshiba on the presentation (best known for voicing Kiki in Kiki’s Delivery Service) to share her appreciation for the Pikmin franchise (she likes to knit Pikmin hats that she shares on social media) and introduce a Pikmin short film. In the short, a Pikmin interacts with a toad, but I won’t spoil what happens. Miyamoto promised more shorts are on the way and in the future, they will be found in the Nintendo Today app.

Unfortunately, the stream concluded without a single reference to 2017's Hey! Pikmin. I wouldn't expect it to get a port to Switch 2 anytime soon.

#4202. Round Up: The Reviews Are In For The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time On Switch 2

The week is finally upon us, folks! We are less than 24 hours away from the launch of Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, and to say that we're all excited would be an understatement.

Our excitement is made all the bigger by the fact that the game's reviews are now in, so we can start to get an idea of what the full experience has in store for us.

Here at Nintendo Life, the sublime Ollie Reynolds awarded Link's latest a 9/10, calling it a "very safe remake," but "comfortably the most visually stunning work Nintendo has ever put out, and it’s unquestionably the best way to play one of the most seminal games of all time". Here's a brief snippet followed by a link to the full thing:

The visuals, the gameplay, the audio – everything has been thoughtfully upgraded to such a degree that this will completely replace the original for many. While the lack of Master Quest means it falls short of being definitive, it's still a remarkable remake, and a must-buy for Switch 2.

Review The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time (Switch 2) - A Stunning Remake, But Not Quite Definitive

But of course, we're not alone in our thoughts. Reviews have now gone live across many outlets, so we have assembled the following roundup to give you an idea of the spread of critical opinions as it stands (spoiler: there's not all that much of a spread).

We'll start with a few full-beans scores. The first comes from GamesRadar, with a 5/5 review that calls it "a reimagining bigger and bolder than any I've ever played before it":

It's as timeless as it ever was, managing to recreate one of the most beautiful games to date without compromising the magic of its 1998 predecessor – only adding to it

VGC also came in with a 5/5, praising "how little has been lost in translation" between the remake and the original:

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was already one of gaming’s most essential experiences, and this wonderful restoration makes it the definitive way to discover – or rediscover – a masterpiece

And Eurogamer followed suit with another 5/5:

This is Ocarina as it's always been, as timeless and intricate, but it also has a vibrancy and clarity that makes it feel like it was just created last Wednesday

Things drop ever so slightly (perhaps thanks only to the bump to a bigger review score range) in Game Informer's 9.25 review:

I was rarely surprised during my playthrough, but I was incredibly excited to see old friends and I happily share without embarrassment that playing through its final hour made me cry

By approaching this remake with a degree of reverence and respect for the source material, Nintendo has shown that a true masterpiece can stand the test of time

This remake proves there’s still so much value in the traditional Zelda formula: the dense, intimate world of Hyrule is stuffed with charming characters and fascinating secrets

And finally, just in the interest of showing the odd lower score out there, RPG Site awarded the remake an 8/10:

#4201. 35 million of you have already pre-registered for Arknights: Endfield

Ahead of its official release next week, Arknights: Endfield has already surpassed 35 million pre-registrations from players around the world.

Arknights: Endfield developer Gryphline has a good reason to celebrate, as the upcoming free-to-play action RPG has achieved yet another milestone. The developer announced today that Endfield already has over 35 million pre-registrations.

This a major moment for the game, which is poised to be one of 2026’s biggest releases on mobile.

In December, when Gryphline officially revealed the Arknights: Endfield release date, the developer said at the time that the game had surpassed 30 million pre-registrations, meaning over 5 million more have joined in since then.

Arknights: Endfield has pretty much wrapped up closed testing, and we’re in the final stretch ahead of the January 22 launch, when the free-to-play game will go live across PC (where it'll be available via the Epic Games Store, as well as Gryphline's own launcher), PS5, and mobile platforms (iOS, Android).

The developer hosted a livestream to celebrate, where it also debuted two new trailers: the launch trailer (below), as well as another look at gameplay. The gameplay trailer also shows off more of the game’s Talos-2 world, and sets up the mystery at the centre of its narrative.

If you’re going to be playing Endfield on PC, you’ll be happy to know that you can expert a breezy experience with support for 120fps. The game also comes with a wide range of modern technologies, including Nvidia DLSS Super Resolution, and Frame Generation. Both Xbox and PlayStation controllers are supported, too.

You can expect more Arknights: Endfield coverage from us at release and beyond. In fact, based on what we played so far, we’re pretty confident in this early Arknights Endfield characters list.

#4200. Former Xbox COO Issues Lengthy Departure Statement To 'Set The Record Straight'

"This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end."

This time last week, we mentioned how newly-promoted Xbox Chief Operating Officer Helen Chiang was suddenly leaving Microsoft after 21 years, with a suggestion at the time that she may have been "terminated for policy violations".

Chiang has now taken to LinkedIn to share a lengthy departure statement in which she denies she was fired for a policy violation, but nevertheless suggests concerns regarding how certain things were handled in her case.

The statement does the talking for itself, so we'll share it in full down below:

"Clarity is Kindness There has been some speculation about my abrupt departure from Microsoft, including claims that I was “fired for a policy violation”. That’s not accurate and while I won’t turn this into a play-by-play, silence should not be mistaken for agreement. What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize. It’s important to me to set the record straight. First, I did not leak confidential company information to the press. I have never communicated with any journalist outside the limited, company-authorized interviews I’ve done as part of my job. That includes every journalist who reached out this week seeking my side of the story. Second, I did not leave XBOX to join a competitor. You don’t spend two decades somewhere without developing a deep loyalty to the people, teams, and businesses you’ve helped build. XBOX was never just another stop in my career. My end game was always to keep building here. Third, I did not engage in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity. I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career. I won’t let speculation define my character or erase that record. Lastly, I did not leave because I was passed over for a bigger role. Since having children, I’ve been intentional about how I define ambition and success. I haven’t actively sought out bigger roles or increased responsibilities, and the last time I interviewed for a job was in 2011. My reputation and results paved the way for the opportunities that followed. I went where the company believed I was needed and where I could have the greatest impact. I did not ask for my most recent role, either. I was promoted into it in July. I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously. I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That’s the legacy I hope to leave behind. To everyone who has reached out with hugs, love, and support: thank you. So many of you have reminded me of the wonderful times we’ve shared over the past 20 years and the impact we’ve had on one another. Some of you I haven’t been in touch with for several years, yet you still took the time to check on me. Others are people I’ve never even met, but you reached out anyway. That speaks volumes about the care and humanity in our industry and the connections that transcend where we work. This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end. And it is not the whole story."

As you can see, Chiang starts her statement here with the phrase "clarity is kindness", which is a phrase that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has used on numerous occasions since taking her role a few months ago.

Nothing specific is said about why Chiang was let go (or potentially decided to leave) as part of this statement though, and while she's certainly assertive in getting her point across, there's no evident malice directed at anyone.

Ultimately, she says she's publishing this statement to avoid being linked to "incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal", and that her story is about "staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard".

On behalf of everyone at Pure Xbox, we wish Chiang all the best in her future endeavours.

#4199. Yakuza Creator Toshiro Nagoshi's Studio Has Officially Shut Down, Ending Gang Of Dragon's Development With It

Nagoshi Studio, the developer led by Yakuza/Like a Dragon series creator Toshiro Nagoshi, has officially shut down, ending development of Gang of Dragon, which was revealed at The Game Awards last year. Shareholders resolved to dissolve the studio on October 31, according to a notice published in a Japanese government newspaper called Kanpo, as first reported by Gematsu.

This follows a report from Bloomberg earlier this year that said Chinese gaming megacorp NetEase Games was cutting funding to Nagoshi Studio, allowing Nagoshi to seek independent funding elsewhere. It seems he couldn't find funding, and now Nagoshi Studio is no more. NetEase helped Nagoshi found the studio in November 2021.

You can watch the Gang of Dragon reveal trailer below for a look at what the team was cooking up:

This closure follows other signals that NetEase is looking to divest from the gaming scene outside of its Chinese studios. A little over a month ago, Suda51's Grasshopper Manufacture left NetEase to go independent again, just months after the launch of Romeo Is A Dead Man.

#4198. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.

#4197. Heartopia surprise launches on Steam and shockingly, everyone seems to be happy

Heartopia players didn't actually end up having to wait too long to play the game on Steam, which is certainly not what anyone expected.

Heartopia has officially arrived on Steam, only a little over a week after it launched on iOS and Android. When the game’s release date was announced back in December, developer XD said it was pushing back the Steam release without offering any hints about how long the delay was going to be.

While the game can be played on PC through TapTap, the developer’s own emulator, many had been anticipating the Steam launch. So you can imagine that when the free-to-play life sim game surprisingly showed up on Valve’s platform on Saturday, there were a lot of happy people.

Heartopia’s Steam release has, much like mobile launch, been a success. We do know that the game reached the number one spot across app stores in over 50 countries, and though the Steam numbers may not be as record-breaking, everything is looking pretty good.

The game peaked at a decent 28,815 concurrent players (via SteamDB) on Steam one day after it launched, and considering how sticky it has been with the majority of those players so far - and the fact the launch itself was a surprise - there’s every chance those figures will improve over the course of this week as it picks up momentum.

Steam user reviews have similarly been quite positive, with the overall rating currently sitting at Mostly Positive, based on over 1,400 reviews.

You’re still need either a Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log into the game, same as you would on mobile. The Steam version does support cross-play with other platforms, so you’ll be able to play with your friends on mobile.

We’ve been playing a lot of Heartopia ourselves, and have been updating and expanding our guides. If you’re looking to get started, such as with how to add and play with friends, how to regain Energy, and how to unlock home plots, our guides offer the best place to start.

Once you’re past the initial hump, you’ll probably be looking for where to find things like mushrooms, bugs, fish, and birds, so definitely bookmark those, too. If you simply like free stuff, our Heartopia codes page is a must read before playing.

Sacrilicious Treats Heartopia Wonder Egg Hunt: All egg locations

#4196. 101 Rapid-Fire Questions With The Exodus Team

Exodus is set in a far-flung future, with humankind stretching out to the stars and exploring a whole new realm of possibilities. This, of course, means we have quite a few questions about what's happening in the universe surrounding Archetype Entertainment's RPG.

As part of our cover story coverage, we sat down with three members of Exodus' leadership team to ask them some rapid-fire questions. Will there be romance? Will there be cool weapons? Will there be cheesy glove-based puns? Does Sega's incredibly influential role-playing saga Phantasy Star get a shout-out? All this and more in the latest Game Informer Rapid-Fire interview with the leadership of Exodus.
